explanation: Microscope is used for the study of micro and nearby objects. Microscope is an instrument that produces enlarged images of small objects, allowing the observer an exceedingly close view of minute structures at a scale convenient for examination and analysis.

To measure the capacity of building

subject: Science & Technology
question: Some pair of devices and associated energy changes are given below: (i) Electric generator – Mechanical to electrical (ii) Electric motor – Electrical to mechanical (iii) Diesel engine – Light to electrical (iv) Solar cell – Chemical to mechanical Which of the following pair/s is /are correctly matched?

subject: Science & Technology
question: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Force has magnitude as well as direction. Statement II: Sliding friction is smaller than static friction. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

question: Which of the following quantity is not a vector?
explanation: Vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. Example – Displacement, Acceleration, Force, Momentum, etc. A scalar quantity has only magnitude. Example- Volume, Energy, Pressure, Work, Distance, Time, Speed etc.

question: Swimming is possible on account of which of the following
explanation: Swimming is possible on account of Newton's third law of motion since as we push water we feel equal force by water on us and we move forward. Third law of motion says that for every action there is equal and opposite reaction.
source: Sikkim PSC (Pre) 2022 · General Science & Technology GS p.12

subject: Science & Technology
question: Assertion (A) : Most of the time individual rain drops hit the earth’s surface with constant velocities. Reason (R): When an object falls through a viscous fluid, it attains a constant terminal velocity after sometime.

explanation: Time = orTime = Speed Velocity SI unit of time is second (s).

subject: Science & Technology
question: In how many cases can the three equations of motion be applied? (I) In one dimensional motion (II) In circular motion (III) Simple harmonic motion (IV) When acceleration is constant
explanation: Equation of motion is applicable when the acceleration is constant. Equations of motion, in physics, are defined as equations that describe the behaviour of a physical system in terms of its motion as a function of time.
source: J & K PSC 2021 Paper-(I) · General Science & Technology GS p.13

subject: Science & Technology
question: When a body falls freely towards the earth, then its total energy:
explanation: The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor be destroyed although it may be transformed from one form to another form. When a body falls freely towards the earth. Its potential energy starts converting into the kinetic energy and the total energy of the body remains same.

subject: Science & Technology
question: When electrical energy converts into motion then-
options: There is no loss of energy
There is a loss of 50 percent energy
There is a loss of 30 percent energy
There is a loss of 80 percent energy
explanation: As per law of conservation of energy, when electrical energy is converted into motion, there is no loss of energy.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2004-05 · General Science & Technology GS p.13

subject: Science & Technology
question: A rocket functions on which of the following laws?
explanation: Rocket functions on the Newton's Third Law of Motion. According to this law, for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. The engine produces hot exhaust gases which flow out of the back of the engine. In reaction, resulting thrusting force is produced in the opposite direction of action. Physics
source: PCS (OSC) Pre 2018 Tripura TPSC Pre-2019 · General Science & Technology GS p.13

subject: Science & Technology
question: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. This law was given by:
explanation: Newton’s First Law of Motion- The first law states that if an object is at rest then it will be at rest and if the object is in motion then it will remain in motion, unless an external force is applied on it. Newton's Second Law of Motion - The second law states that the rate of change of momentum of a body with respect to time is directly proportional to the applied force on it. Newton’s Third Law of Motion- It states that “for every action, there is always an equal and opposite reaction.”
source: UPPSC RO/ARO Mains 2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.13

subject: Science & Technology
question: The four fundamental forces in the universe are-
options: Strong force, weak force, electric and magnetic forces
Electric, magnetic, electromagnetic forces and dark matter
Strong force, weak force, gravity and electromagnetic force
Electric, magnetic, gravitational and strong forces
explanation: The four fundamental forces in universe are – Gravitational force, electromagnetic force, and strong and weak Nuclear forces. These force are responsible for shaping the universe we inhabit.
source: Mizoram PSC-2021 · General Science & Technology GS p.13

subject: Science & Technology
question: Energy conservation means-
options: Energy could be created but cannot be destroyed
Energy could not be created but destroyed
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed
explanation: Whenever energy gets transformed, the total energy remains unchanged. This is the law of conservation of energy. According to this law, energy can only be converted from one form to another; it can neither be created or destroyed. The total energy before and after the transformation remains the same. The law of conservation of energy is valid in all situations and for all kinds of transformations. 17. Assertion (A): A passenger tends to fall forward when a moving train slows down quickly. Reason (R): The lower portion of his body is no longer in touch with the seat as the train stops. A. Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). B. Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). C. (A) is true but (R) is false D. (A) is false but (R) is true Manipur PSC - 2013 Ans. (c): Assertion (A) – A passenger tends to fall forward when a moving train slows down quickly because of the ‘Law of Inertia’. The reason is that when we are moving in the train, we are also moving with the speed of train but when the train stops we are still moving because the part of body which is in contact (lower portion of body) with train comes to rest but the upper part of the body remains in the motion so we lean forward. The Law of Inertia states that, an object will continue to be in the state of rest or in a state of motion unless an external force acts on it. While the Reason (R) is false. Hence option (c) is the right answer.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 2000 · General Science & Technology GS p.13

subject: Science & Technology
question: Ball bearings are used in bicycles, cars, etc., because-
options: The actual area of contact between the wheels and axle is increased
The effective area of contact between the wheels and axle is increased
The effective area of contact between the wheels and axle is reduced
None of the above statementsst is correct
explanation: Ball bearing are used in bicycles to reduce friction. Friction is reduced by reducing the effective area of contact between the wheels and axle.
source: IAS (Pre) I Paper G.S. 2013 · General Science & Technology GS p.14

subject: Science & Technology
question: A car is running on a road at a uniform speed of 60 km/hr. The net resultant force on the car is
options: Driving force in the direction of car's motion
Resistance force opposite to the direction of car's motion
explanation: Newton’s Second Law of Motion states that “The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and momentum takes place in the direction in which the force acts.” Since the car is moving at a uniform speed thus rate of change of momentum is zero. Hence the net resultant force on car is zero.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2004 · General Science & Technology GS p.14

subject: Science & Technology
question: A spherical body moves with a uniform angular velocity ( ω) around a circular path of radius r. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The body has a radial acceleration ( ω² r) directed towards the centre of the path
The body has a radial acceleration ( 2/3 ω² r) directed away from the centre of the path
The body has an acceleration ( ω² r) tangential to its path
explanation: In a uniform circular motion, the acceleration of the object is along the radius directed towards the center and is₂ called radial acceleration. Radial Acceleration = v /r where v is linear velocity and r is radius of the circular path. From, v = ωr Therefore, Radial acceleration= v² /r = ω² r
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2004 · General Science & Technology GS p.14

subject: Science & Technology
question: An oil tanker is partially filled with oil and moves forward on a level road with uniform acceleration. The free surface of oil then: Physics 2
options: is inclined to the horizontal with smaller depth at the rear end
is inclined to the horizontal with larger depth at the rear end
explanation: As tanker moves with uniform acceleration on level road, force will be exerted on the oil at the rear end. So it will be inclined to the horizontal with larger depth at rear end.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2003 · General Science & Technology GS p.14

subject: Science & Technology
question: ‘A’ and ‘B’ are two fixed points in a field. A cyclist ‘C’ moves such that ACB is always a right angle. In this context, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The path followed by the cyclist is an ellipse
The path followed by the cyclist is a circle

source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2003 · General Science & Technology GS p.14

subject: Science & Technology
question: Consider the following statements: A 4-wheel vehicle moving in a sharp circular path at high speed will: 1. Overturn about its outer wheels. 2. Overturn about its inner wheels 3. Skid outwards 4. Skid inwards Which of these statements is/are correct?
explanation: If an object is moving on a circular path, two type of forces namely centripetal force and centrifugal force act upon it. As these two forces act in opposite direction, object remains in balance. When a four wheel vehicle moving at high speed reaches at sharp circular path, the centrifugal force gets unbalanced. Therefore the vehicle will overturn about its inner wheel and skid outwards.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2003 · General Science & Technology GS p.14

subject: Science & Technology
question: Consider the following statements: A simple pendulum is set into oscillation. Then 1. The acceleration is zero when the bob passes through the mean position 2. In each cycle the bob attains a given velocity twice 3. Both acceleration and velocity of the bob are zero when it reaches its extreme position during its oscillation 4. The amplitude of oscillation of the simple pendulum decreases with time Which of these statements are correct?
explanation: If a simple pendulum is set into oscillation then the acceleration is zero, when the bob passes through the mean position (displacement is zero). In each cycle the bob attains a given velocity twice and the amplitude of oscillation of the simple pendulum decreases with time. At extreme positions velocity would be zero but due to maximum force acceleration would be maximum.
source: IAS (Pre) GS-2001 · General Science & Technology GS p.15

question: A simple machine helps a person doing:

The same amount of work much faster

source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1996 · General Science & Technology GS p.15

subject: Science & Technology
question: A girl is swinging on a swing in sitting position. When the same girl stands up, the period of swing will-
options: Depend on the height of the girl
explanation: Time period of oscillation of a simple l pendulum is (T) = 2π where l is length of simple g pendulum. Length of simple pendulum is equal to distance from point of suspension to center of gravity (C.G) of the oscillating body. When the girl stands up, the distance of center of gravity from point of suspension decreases. Therefore time period of oscillation or period of swing will also decreases.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1997 · General Science & Technology GS p.15

question: Pendulum clock becomes slow in summer because:

The length of the pendulum increases
The weight of the pendulum changes
explanation: Time period of oscillation of a simple l pendulum is (T) = 2π g ⇒ T ∝ l During summer, the length of pendulum increases due to the thermal expansion. As the length increases, the time period (T) increases and pendulum takes more time to complete one oscillation. So the pendulum clock becomes slow in summer. During winters, length decreases, then due to decrease in the time period the clock becomes fast.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1994, 2012 · General Science & Technology GS p.15

question: Pendulum clock could move faster-

subject: Science & Technology
question: The time period of pendulum depends upon-
explanation: The time period of pendulum depends upon the length of the pendulum. If the length of the pendulum increases then the time period of the pendulum will increase.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2004-05 · General Science & Technology GS p.15

subject: Science & Technology
question: A man jumped at a speed of 5 meters per second from a stationary boat and the boat moved off with the speed of 0.5 meter per second. How many times is the mass of the boat greater than that of the man?
explanation: Let the mass of the man is M and the mass of the boat is m, then momentum of boat +momentum of man before jump is zero. Momentum of both after man’s jump = M × .5 – m × 5 M × .5 – m × 5 = 0 (due to principle of conservation of momentum) M×5 = m×0.5 M 5 ⇒ = =10 m .5 So, mass of the boat is 10 time greater than that of the man. Hence the correct option is (d).

subject: Science & Technology
question: The jet aircraft flies very easily and smoothly in the lower stratosphere. What could be the appropriate explanation? (i) There are no clouds or water vapour in the lower stratosphere (ii) There are no vertical winds in the lower stratosphere Which of the above explanation is/are correct in this context?
explanation: Stratosphere is the second layer of atmosphere. The bottom of Stratosphere is around 10 km. The top of Stratosphere occurs at an altitude of 50 km. The stratosphere is very dry and air contains little water vapour. Because of this, few clouds are found in this layer. Because the temperature in the lower stratosphere is largely constant with increasing altitude, very little convection (vertical wind) occurs. So the jet aircraft flies very easily and smoothly in the lower stratosphere.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. II Paper 2013 · General Science & Technology GS p.16

subject: Science & Technology
question: A man is standing on a boat in the still water. If he moves towards the corner, then the boat would -

question: One person is sitting in a train having his face towards engine. When he tosses a coin, it fall to its back. Train is moving:

question: As the train starts moving, the head of the passenger sitting inside leans backwards because of-

subject: Science & Technology
question: The energy of wind is-
explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion. The kinetic energy of an object increases with its speed. Hence energy of wind is kinetic energy.
source: Uttarakhand Lower (Pre) 2011 · General Science & Technology GS p.16

subject: Science & Technology
question: In wind power, which form of energy is converted into electrical energy?
explanation: Wind is used to produce electricity using the kinetic energy created by air in motion. This is transformed into electrical energy using wind turbines or wind energy conversion systems. Wind first hits a turbine’s blades, causing them to rotate and turn the turbine connected to them. That changes the kinetic energy to rotational energy by moving a shaft which is connected to a generator and thereby producing electrical energy through electromagnetism.

source: UPPSC Asst. Forest Eam.-2013 Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2004-05 · General Science & Technology GS p.17

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which physical unit can be obtained by the ratio of momentum and velocity?
explanation: The momentum, P of an object is defined as the product of its mass, m and velocity, v. i.e., p = mv. Momentum has both direction and magnitude. Its direction is the same as that of velocity, v. The SI unit₋₁ of momentum is kilogram-meter per second (kgms). Therefore the physical quantity ‘mass’ can be obtained by the ratio of momentum and velocity.
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 2002 · General Science & Technology GS p.17

subject: Science & Technology
question: Force is multiple of:
explanation: Force F = Mass₋₂ × Acceleration = ma. The unit of force is kg-ms or Newton, which has the symbol N.
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 2002 · General Science & Technology GS p.17

subject: Science & Technology
question: In which branch of physics, the speed of very small particles is studied?

source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S., 2003 · General Science & Technology GS p.17

subject: Science & Technology
question: When the velocity of a movable object is doubled then its kinetic energy would be-
explanation: Kinetic energy of an object (K.E.) = mv If velocity is doubled, then 1₂ 1₂ Kinetic energy = m(2v) = m×4v 2 2 1₂ = 4× mv = 4×K.E. Hence if the velocity is doubled, kinetic energy will be four times.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Batsman hits a cricket ball which then rolls on a level ground. After covering a short distance, the ball comes to rest. The ball slows to a stop because:
options: The batsman did not hit the ball hard enough
Velocity is proportional to the force exerted on the ball
There is a force on the ball opposing the motion
There is no unbalanced force on the ball, so the ball would try to come to rest
explanation: When the ball rolls on the ground, two forces namely friction and air resistance applies on the ball in opposite direction of motion. These two forces oppose the motion of the ball.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following statements is false?
options: A body can have zero velocity and still be accelerated
A body can have a constant velocity and a varying speed
A body can have a constant speed and a varying velocity
The direction of the velocity of a body can change when its acceleration is constant
explanation: A body cannot have its velocity constant, while its speed varies. Rather, it can have its speed constant and its velocity varying for example in a uniform circular motion. question: Consider the following Statement Statement I : The universal gravitational constant G is important because it determines the strength of one of the four forces in nature. options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

subject: Science & Technology

subject: Science & Technology
question: The mass of a body on Earth is 100₂ kg (acceleration due to gravity, ge = 10 m/s). If acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is ge /6, then the mass of the body on the moon is:
explanation: Mass is measure of amount of matter in a body. Mass of a body does not change at any place. Therefore mass of the body on moon would remain same i.e. 100kg. subject: Science & Technology
question: Who formulated the universal law of gravitation?
explanation: Newton formulated the universal law of gravitation. It states that every object in the universe attracts each other with a force which is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. The force is along the line joining the centers of two objects. The law of universal gravitation applies uniformly in the sense that it is applicable to all bodies, whether the bodies are big or small, whether they are celestial or terrestrial. Where M is mass of object A and m is mass of object B, d is distance between the two objects. G is universal gravitation constant. The accepted value of G is 6.673 × 10 –11 N m² kg –2

subject: Science & Technology
question: Consider the following statements: If there was no phenomenon of capillarity 1. It would be difficult to use a kerosene lamp 2. One would not be able to use a straw to consume a soft drink 3. The blotting paper would fail to function 4. The big trees that we see around would not have grown on the Earth Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Capillarity action is the ability of a liquids to flow in narrow spaces without the assistance of, or even in opposition to external forces like gravity. It occurs because of intermolecular forces between the liquid and surroundings solid surfaces. If the diameter of tube is sufficiently small, then the combination of surface tension and adhesive forces between the liquid and container wall act to propel the liquid. Kerosene rises in the wick of lamp through capillary action. Blotting paper has large number of pores on its surface which acts as capillary tube. Capillary action helps to bring water up into the tree roots. For consuming a soft drink through straw, a person needs to impose some external pressure by his mouth. Here capillary action has no role to play.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S, 2012 · General Science & Technology GS p.23

question: For which one of the following is capillarity not the only reason?

Rising of water from the roots of a plant to its foliage

Capillary action helps bring water up into the tree roots. But capillary action can only pull water up a small distance after which it cannot overcome gravity, to get water up to all the branches and leaves, the forces of adhesion and cohesion works in the plant's xylem to move water to the farthest leaf (foliage).

subject: Science & Technology
question: Two statements have been given below. One of them is called Assertion (A) and second one is called Reason (R). Assertion (A): With the increase of temperature, the viscosity of glycerin increases. Reason (R): Rise of temperature increases kinetic energy of molecules. Select the correct answer using the codes given below: Code:
options: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Most of the fluids are not ideal ones and offer some resistance to motion. This resistance to fluid motion is like an internal friction analogous to friction when a solid moves on a surface. It is called viscosity. This force exists when there is relative motion between layers of the liquid. The viscosity of liquids decreases with increase in temperature while it increases in the case of gases. As glycerin is a liquid, therefore its viscosity will decrease with increase in temperature. Hence statement (A) is false. The average kinetic energy of the gas molecules is proportional to the temperature of the gas. Therefore rise in temperature will increase the kinetic energy of molecules. Hence reason (R) is true.

subject: Science & Technology
question: To hear a clear echo, the minimum distance between the reflecting surface and the observer should be?
explanation: If we shout or clap near a suitable reflecting object such as a tall building or a mountain, we will hear the same sound again a little. This sound which we hear is called an echo. To hear a distinct echo the time interval between the original sound and the reflected one must be at least 0.1 second. If we take the speed of sound to be 330 m/s at a given temperature, the sound must go to the obstacle and reach back the ear of the listener on reflection after 0.1 second. Hence, the total distance covered by the sound from the point of generation to the reflecting surface and back should be at least (330 m/s) × 0.1 s = 33 m. Thus, for hearing distinct echoes, the minimum distance of the obstacle from the source of sound must be half of this distance, that is, 16.5 meters. This distance will change with the temperature of air.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. II Paper 2007 · General Science & Technology GS p.32

question: Consider the following₀ statements:₀ 1. Steam at 100 C and boiling water at 100 C contain same amount of heat. 2. Latent heat of fusion of ice is equal to the latent heat of vaporization of water 3. In an air-conditioner, heat is extracted from the room-air at the evaporator coils and is rejected out at the condenser coils. Which of these statements is/are correct?
explanation: The amount of heat per unit mass transferred during change of state of the substance is called latent heat₅ of the substance. Steam at 100 °C carries 22.6 × 10 J kg –1 more heat than water at 100 °C. This is why burns from steam are usually more serious than those from boiling water. Hence statement one is not correct. The latent heat for a solid to liquid state change is called the latent heat of fusion and that for a liquid to gas state change is called the latent heat of vaporization. Latent heat of fusion of ice is approximately 80 calories per gram while latent heat of vaporization of water is about 536 calories per gram. Hence statement two is also incorrect. An air conditioning system has two coils, condenser coils and evaporator coils usually made of copper tubes with aluminium fins. The evaporator coil or indoor coil is often described as the cold coil because it provides indoor cooling. The coil works by absorbing heat from the indoor air that is blown over by the air handler’s fan. The condenser coil or outdoor coil is the warm coil as it rejects the heat as a fan blows outside air over the surface. Hence statement three is correct.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2003 · General Science & Technology GS p.38

In a double rainbow, a second arc is seen outside the primary arc and the order of its colours is reversed with red on the bottom and violet on the top. So both the marginal spectrum of a rain bow is violet and red. This is caused by light being reflected twice inside the droplets before leaving it. When the white light is passing through a glass prism it splits into its spectrum of colours (violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red) (VIBGYOR) and this process of white light splitting into its constituent colours is termed as dispersion. The different colours in the spectrum of light have different wavelengths. Therefore the speed with which they all bend varies depending on this wavelength. Violet having the shortest wavelength, bends the most, and red having the longest wavelength, bends the least.

question: Two statements are given below. One is assertion (A) and second is reason (R). Assertion (A) : Small glass beads fixed on traffic signals glow brightly when light falls upon them. Reason (R): Light is totally reflected when the angle of incidence exceeds a certain critical value and light traveling in a denser medium is reflected from a rarer medium. Code:
options: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is NOT a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Small glass beads fixed on traffic signals glow brightly when light falls upon them due to the phenomenon of total internal reflection. When light travels from an optically denser medium to a rarer medium at the interface, it is partly reflected back into the same medium and partly refracted to the second medium. This reflection is called the internal reflection. If the angle of incidence is increased to a certain critical value, refraction is not possible and the incident ray is totally reflected. This is called total internal reflection. Hence Both A and R are Individually true and R is the correct explanation of A.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2000 · General Science & Technology GS p.51

question: When a CD (compact disc used in audio and video systems) is seen in sunlight, rainbow like colours are seen. This can be explained on the basis of the phenomenon of:
explanation: The reason CDs reflect rainbow colors is because they have a clear plastic coating on top of a mirrorized surface. Light refracts (bends) when it moves from one medium (such as air) to another with a different optical density (such as the clear plastic surface of a CD). Different wave lengths of light (every color has a different wave length) travel at different speeds, so that full spectrum appears when white light passes from the air through the plastic surface of a CD, separated light rays which are then reflected back to us by the mirrorized centre surface of a CD. Here the diffraction and transmission also takes place because diffraction of light rays occur when it strikes the surface of CD and transmission is obvious when light enters from one medium to another the thickness of the different optical media, angle of source light and brightness of source light all affect when rainbow patterns are visible on a CD.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2000 · General Science & Technology GS p.51

subject: Science & Technology
question: Blue colour of the sky is due to:
options: Emission of more blue light as compared to other colours by the sun
explanation: The molecules of air and other fine particles (dust) in the atmosphere have smaller size and scatter visible light. These are more effective in scattering light of shorter wavelengths at the blue than light of longer wavelengths at the red. The red light has a wavelength about 1.8 times greater than blue light. Thus when sunlight passes through the atmosphere, the fine particles in air scatter the blue colour (shorter wavelengths) more strongly than red. The scattered blue light enters our eyes and we feels the colour of sky blue. If the earth had no atmosphere, there would not have been no scattering. Then the sky would have looked black or dark. The sky appears black or dark to passengers flying at very high altitudes as scattering is not prominent at such heights.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Re-exam. 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.53

explanation: Natural uranium found in the earth's crust is a mixture largely of two isotopes: uranium-238 (U- 238), accounting for 99.3% and uranium-235 (U-235) about 0.7%. The isotope U-235 is important because under certain conditions it can readily be split, yielding a lot of energy. The nucleus of the U-235 atom comprises 92 protons and 143 neutrons. When the nucleus of a U-235 atom captures a moving neutron it splits in two fissions starts and releases some energy in the form of heat and two or three additional neutrons are thrown off. If enough of these expelled neutrons cause the nuclei of other U-235 atoms to split, releasing further neutrons, a fission chain reaction can be achieved. When this happens over and over again, a very large amount of heat is produced from a relatively small amount of uranium. Hence U-235 is used in nuclear power plants to produce electricity.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) I 2014-15 · General Science & Technology GS p.72

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which is used to prevent rusting in iron?
explanation: Galvanizing is a method of rust prevention. The iron or steel object is coated with a thin layer of zinc. This stops oxygen and water reaching the metal underneath. In addition to that, the zinc also acts as a sacrificial metal. Zinc is more reactive than iron so it oxidizes in preference to the iron object. Other methods to prevent iron rusting are- 1. Use an alloy- like stainless steal by using chromium. 2. Apply oil 3. Dry coating with preventive products. 4. Paint the metal. 5. Bluing - it creates a layer of magnetite over the metal. But it need regular oiling to maintain rust resistance, and it will turn blue or black in the process.

subject: Science & Technology

explanation: Pasteurization is a process of heating of milk or wine and sudden cooling to make it safe from pathogen or harmful microbes. For example - Sterilization of milk. Pasteurized milk can be consumed without boiling as it is free₀ from harmful microbes. The milk is heated to about 70 C for 15 to 30 seconds and then suddenly cooled and stored. By doing so, it prevents the growth of microbes. In low temperature long time pasteurization, the temperatures used for pasteurization are reduced to 63°C and held for 30 minutes. Pasteurization process was discovered by Louis Pasteur.

explanation: If we add a little water to a lot of concentrated acid, the resulting solution is still concentrated. The hydration reaction uses all the water, generating a lot of heat. explanation: Ionization energy is the minimum amount of energy required to remove an electron from the ground state of an atom or ion. Ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period. Hence statement 1 is incorrect. Electron affinity is the energy change incurred from gaining an electron. Therefore electron affinity decreases as the atomic weight increases. Hence statement 2 is correct. Electronegativity is the ability of an atom in a molecule to attract electrons to itself. explanation: Baking soda is the main constituent of dry chemical fire extinguisher. Limestone (Calcium Carbonate) is one of the main components in glass manufacturing. explanation: Anodizing is a process of forming a thick oxide layer of aluminium. Aluminium develops a thin oxide layer when exposed to air. This aluminium oxide coating makes it resistant to further corrosion. During anodizing, a clean aluminium article is made the anode and is electrolyzed with dilute sulphuric acid. The oxygen gas evolved at the anode reacts with aluminium to make a thicker protective oxide layer. This oxide layer can be dyed easily to give aluminium articles an attractive finish.

question: The metallurgical process in which a metal is obtained in a fused state is called:

Extrusion is a process where a material undergoes plastic deformation by the application of a force causing that material to flow through an orifice or die. Froth flotation is a process that selectively separates materials based upon whether they are water repelling (hydrophobic) or have an affinity for water (hydrophilic).

They are concentrated in a particular area or rock formation. Minerals are formed in different types of geological environments under varying conditions. They are created by natural processes without any human interference. They can be identified on the basis of their physical properties such as colour, density, hardness and chemical property such as solubility.

question: In the context of proposals to the use of hydrogen-enriched CNG (H-CNG) as fuel for buses in public transport, consider the following statements: 1. subject: Science & Technology
question: With reference to 'fuel cells' in which hydrogen- rich fuel and oxygen are used to generate electricity. Consider the following statements: 1. If pure hydrogen is used as a fuel, the fuel cell emits heat and water as by-products. 2. Fuel cells can be used for powering buildings and not for small devices like laptop computers. 3. Fuel cells produce electricity in the form of Alternating Current (AC). Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: A fuel cell uses the chemical energy of hydrogen or another fuel to produce clean and efficient electricity. If hydrogen is used as a fuel, the fuel cell emits heat and water as by products. Hence statement 1 is correct. Fuel cells are unique in terms of the variety of their potential applications. They can provide power for systems as large as a utility power station and as small as a laptop computer. Hence statement 2 is incorrect. Fuel cells work like batteries but they do not run down or need recharging. They produce electricity and heat as long as fuel is supplied. A fuel cell consists of two electrodes, a negative electrode (or anode) and a positive electrode (or cathode), sandwiched around an electrolyte. A fuel such as hydrogen is to the anode and air is fed to the cathode. Fuel cells produce electricity in the form of direct current (DC). In a DC circuit, electrons flow in only one direction. The electricity in home and workplace is in the form of alternating current (AC), which flows in both directions on alternating cycles. Hence statement 3 is also incorrect.
source: IAS(Pre) I Paper G.S., 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.116

explanation: Biogas is produced after organic materials (plant and animal products) are broken down by bacteria in an oxygen free environment, a process called anaerobic digestion or anaerobic fermentation. Anaerobic digestion already occurs in nature, landfills and some livestock manure management systems but can be optimized, controlled and contained using an anaerobic digester. Biogas contains roughly 50-70 percent methane, 30-40 percent carbon dioxide and trace amounts of other gases. Biogas is not a commercial source. It is mainly used for domestic purpose.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following substances is not synthetic?
explanation: Fibroin is not synthetic. It has been widely used to produce materials for bio medical applications. Silk proteins can be extracted from silk glands or silkworm cocoons. Typically, the fibroin is extracted from the silkworm cocoon by removal of Sericin and is then purified. There are several methods to extract and purify silk fibroin protein. One of the most widely used procedures for the removal of Sericin ("degumming") is Sodium Carbonate boiling and/or autoclaving. The fibroin is then extracted from the degummed silk by dissolving it in a concentrated solution of lithium or sometimes in a ternary solvent system of calcium chloride/ethanol/water.

question: Bisphenol A (BPA), a cause of concern, is a structural/key component in the manufacture of which of the following kinds of plastics?
explanation: Bisphenol A (BPA) is an industrial chemical used to make polycarbonate, a hard, clear plastic, which is used in many consumer products. BPA is also found in epoxy resins, which act as a protective lining on the inside of some metal-based food and beverage cans. Bisphenol A can leach into food from the protective internal epoxy resin coatings of canned foods and from consumer products such as polycarbonate tableware, food storage containers, water bottles, and baby bottles. The degree to which BPA leaches from polycarbonate bottles into liquid may depend more on the temperature of the liquid or bottle, than the age of the container. BPA can also be found in breast milk. One reason people may be concerned about BPA is because human exposure to BPA is widespread. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer. Chemistry
source: UPSC PRE (IAS) 2021 · General Science & Technology GS p.122

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following is not a natural polymer?
explanation: The term polymer is defined as very large molecules having high molecular mass. These are also referred to as macromolecules which are formed by joining of repeating structural units on a large scale. The repeating structural units are derived from some simple and reactive molecules known as monomers and are linked to each other by covalent bonds. The process of formation of polymers from respective monomers is called polymerisation. Natural polymers are found in plants and animals such as proteins, cellulose, starch, wool, silk, leather and rubber. Semi synthetic polymers are cellulose derivatives such as cellulose acetate (rayon) and cellulose nitrate. A variety of synthetic polymers as plastic (polythene), synthetic fibres (nylon 6,6) and synthetic rubbers (Buna - S) are examples of the synthetic polymers.

Stimulants speed up mental and physical processes which can produce desirable effects in the short-term by increasing levels of dopamine in the brain. Depressants - also called downers, acts just opposite to stimulants, i.e., decreases the rate of speed of messages passing between body and brain, and so decrease the body activity. Commonly used depressants - Alcohol, Benzodiazepines, GHB (gamma-hydroxybutyrate), Ketamine. All the given options acts as both depressants as well as stimulants. question: Recently, there has been a concern over the short supply of a group of elements called 'rare earth metals'. Why? 1. Other than China, Australia, Canada and Chile, these elements are not found in any country. 3. Rare earth metals are essential for the manufacture of various kinds of electronic items and there is a growing demand for these elements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: The rare earth metals are the set of seventeen metallic elements. These include the fifteen lanthanides on the periodic table plus scandium and Yttrium. In 2011, China accounted 97 percent of the world production of rare earth elements. The Government of China began to change the amount of the Rare Earth Metals that it allows to be produced and exported. The Chinese Government also began to limit the number of Chinese and Sino-foreign joint-venture companies that could export rare earth metals from China. Hence statement 1 is correct. In 1993, 38 percent of world production of rare earth metals was in China, 33 percent was in the United States, 12 percent was in Australia and five percent each was in Malaysia and India. Several other countries, including Brazil, Canada, South Africa, Sri Lanka and Thailand made up the remainder. Hence statement 2 is incorrect. Rare-earth metals are necessary components of more than 200 products across a wide range of applications, especially high-tech consumer products such as cellular telephones, computer hard drives, electric and hybrid vehicles and flat-screen monitors and televisions. Significant defense applications include electronic displays, guidance systems, lasers and radar and sonar systems. Hence statement 3 is correct.

Structure of rocks can be calculated
Colour of the rocks can be calculated
Weight of the rocks can be calculated

subject: Science & Technology
question: What is Bisphenol A (BPA)?
options: A medical test for detecting cancer
A test for testing the use of drugs to improve performance by athletes
A chemical used for the development of food- packaging materials
A special type of alloy steel
explanation: Bisphenol A (BPA) is a chemical produced in large quantities for use primarily in the production of polycarbonate plastics and epoxy resins. Polycarbonate plastics have many applications including use in some food and drink packaging, e.g., as water and infant bottles, compact discs, impact-resistant safety equipment and medical devices. Epoxy resins are used as lacquers to coat metal products such as food cans, bottle tops and water supply pipes.

question: Refrigeration helps in food preservation by

Sealing the food with a layer of ice

explanation: Sedatives are the drugs that can be used to calm down, treat sleep disorders and as a general anesthetic in high doses. Primarily, there are two types of sedatives. 1. Barbiturates - generally not prescribed but still are being used.

question: Rodenticide is a chemical which is used to control-
explanation: Rodenticides are the pesticides that kill rats. Rodents include not only rats and mice but also squirrels, woodchucks, chipmunks, porcupines, nutria and beavers. Commonly used Rodenticide is Zinc Phosphide.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (M) 2002-03 · General Science & Technology GS p.148

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following is used as rat poison?
explanation: Zinc phosphide is an inorganic compound that combines phosphorus with zinc. It is used in rodenticide baits. When an animal eats the bait, the acid in the animal's stomach turns the zinc phosphide into phosphine.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. IInd Paper 2012 · General Science & Technology GS p.148

explanation: Potassium cyanide is the chemical substance that is used for making rat poison. Chemistry

question: Which is most available element in the Earth after oxygen?
explanation: The most abundant element in the earth after oxygen (46.1%) is silicon (28.2%) followed by aluminium (8.23%) and iron (5.63%).

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following elements does not occur in a free state in nature?
explanation: Silicon is the second most abundant element of earth crust after oxygen. Silicon is not found freely in nature but occurs mainly as the oxide and as silicates. Silicon is prepared commercially by heating silica and carbon in an electric furnace, using carbon electrodes.

Utensil is made negatively charged and zinc is made positively charged
Utensil is made positively charged and zinc is made negatively charged
explanation: Zinc electroplating allows coating metals with a physical zinc layer in order to prevent rust from reaching the metal surface underneath. In this process, utensil is made negatively charged and zinc is made positively charged.

subject: Science & Technology

explanation: Sulfur hexafluoride or SF₆ is an inorganic, greenhouse gas. It is a non-flammable, odourless and colourless. It is an excellent insulator. It is a hypervalent octahedral molecule.
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 2002 · General Science & Technology GS p.148

subject: Science & Technology
question: Chromatography technique is used -
options: To determine the structure of compounds
To separate compounds from a mixture
explanation: Chromatography is an important biophysical technique that enables the separation, identification and purification of the components of a mixture for qualitative and quantitative analysis. Chromatography is based on the principle where molecules in mixture form applied onto the surface or into the solid and fluid stationary phase is separating from each other while moving with the aid of a mobile phase.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1997-98 · General Science & Technology GS p.148

explanation: Chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) is responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1997-98 · General Science & Technology GS p.149

subject: Science & Technology
question: An active chemical to remove mosquitoes is-
explanation: Allethrin (C₁₉ H₂₆ O₃) is a cyclopropanecarboxylate ester. It plays a role as a pyrethroid ester insecticide. It is a synthetic household insecticide that kills flies, mosquitoes, garden insects. It derives from chrysanthemic acid.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1996 · General Science & Technology GS p.149

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following is not optically active?
explanation: Glycine is the simplest amino acid and is the only amino acid that is not optically active as it has no stereoisomers. Amino acids contain amino (-NH₂) and carboxyl functional groups (-COOH). Depending on the relative position of amino group, the amino acids can be classified as α, β, γ, δ and so on. Only α-amino acids are obtained on hydrolysis of proteins. They may contain other functional groups also. R − CH − COOH | NH₂ (α-amino acid) R = side chain All amino acids have trivial names, which usually reflect the property of that compound or its source. Glycine is so named since it has sweet taste (in Greeks glykos means sweet) and tyrosine was the first to be obtained from cheese (in Greek tyros means cheese.)
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. IInd Paper, 2013 · General Science & Technology GS p.149

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following elements was first produced artificially?
explanation: Technetium was the first artificially produced element.Technetium was created by bombarding molybdenum atoms with deuterons that had been accelerated by a device called cyclotron.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. IInd Paper, 2013 · General Science & Technology GS p.149

subject: Science & Technology
question: Mica is a ___.
options: Conductor of heat and insulator of electricity
Insulator of both heat and electricity
Conductor of both heat and electricity
Insulator of heat and conductor of electricity
explanation: Mica is a good conductor of heat but is a bad conductor of electricity. It has good thermal conductivity due to phonons but doesn't have sufficient free electrons to conduct electricity.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S., 2003 · General Science & Technology GS p.149

question: Organic foods are considered to be better for us because they are-

Grown without the use of artificial fertilizers and pesticides

source: UP Kanoongo Exam. 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.149

source: UPPSC Asst. Forest Conservator Exam. 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.149

Nickle-Cadmium battery can be used in all the above given gadgets.
source: Uttarakhand PSC (Pre) G.S. 2016 · General Science & Technology GS p.149

subject: Science & Technology
question: Study of Zoology deals with–
explanation: Zoology (also known as animal science) is the branch of biology which deals with the study of animal life. It covers fields ranging from the structure of organisms to the sub cellular unit of life. Aristotle is known as father of Zoology.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1995 · General Science & Technology GS p.150

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following studies come under Paleobotany?
explanation: Paleobotany is the study of fossil plants. A fossil plant is the remains or traces of a once living plant. Fossil plants are generally found buried below ground. Palaeontology is scientific study of life of the geologic past that involves the analysis of plant and animal fossils. Phycology is the scientific study of algae, also known as Algology. Study of fungi is called Mycology. Biology 15 : BIOLOGY . ogy & its Major Branches
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2004-05 · General Science & Technology GS p.150

subject: Science & Technology
question: The study of properties and method of biological systems found in nature and use of this knowledge in mechanical world is known as–
explanation: It is a branch of science on the borderline of art and biology that studies the way living organisms work, as well as their structure, in order to use the results to build technical devices. Bionomics is the study of the mode of life of organisms in their natural habitat and their adaptations to their surroundings. Biometry is the application of statistics, mathematics, computing and other quantitative methods to phenomena and problems in the life sciences.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre.) G.S. 1994-95 · General Science & Technology GS p.150

subject: Science & Technology
question: The branch of science in which human species is improved by genetic engineering, is known as–
explanation: Eugenics can be defined as the application of the principles of genetics and inheritance to the improvement of human race. However it is scientifically erraneous and immoral theory based on racial discrimination. Euthenics is a science concerned with bettering the condition of human beings through the improvement of their environment. Ethnology a branch of cultural anthropology deals with the comparative and analytical study of cultures broadly. Euphenics is a branch of science deals with changing conditions to stop genetic diseases and their harmful effects in individuals.
source: UPPSC Food & Sanitary Inspector Exam. 2013 · General Science & Technology GS p.150

subject: Science & Technology
question: The scientific study of insects is known as:
explanation: Entomology is the study of insects and their relationship to humans, environment, and other organisms. Ichthyology is the branch of zoology devoted to the study of fish. Parasitology is the study of parasites, their hosts, and the relationship between them. Malacology is the branch of zoology that deals with the study of the Molluscs.
source: Uttarakhand UDA (Pre) 2003 · General Science & Technology GS p.150

subject: Science & Technology
question: The branch of study dealing with old age and ageing is called
explanation: Gerontology is the scientific study of older adults and aging. It studies, social, cultural psychological, cognitive and biological aspects of aging. Oncology is the specialized branch of medicine devoted to the field of cancer including study, treatment, diagnosis and prevention. Teratology is branch of the biology dealing with the causes, development, description, and classification of congenital abnormalities in plants and animals.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.151

subject: Science & Technology
question: The viticulture is known as–
explanation: Viticulture is the cultivation and harvesting of grapes. It is a branch of horticulture.

subject: Science & Technology
question: What is Vermiculture?
explanation: Vermiculture refers to the scientific process of cultivating worm or artificial rearing of worms to decompose organic food wastes into a nutrient-rich material.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.151

subject: Science & Technology
question: A branch of science that encompasses the description, identification, nomenclature, and classification of organisms is called -
explanation: Taxonomy is the science of naming, describing and classifying organisms. The term ‘‘taxonomy’’ is derived from two Greek words, ‘‘taxis’’, meaning order or arrangement and ‘‘nomia’’ meaning 'distribution. It is essential to classify living organisms into different groups and sub-groups.
source: Mizoram PSC (CCE) 2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.151

question: Which one of the following pair is correctly matched? (Branch of medicine) (Human organ)
explanation: Cardiology is related to heart, Gastroenterology is related to stomach and intestine, Urology is related to urinary system and Neurology is related to nervous system. Thus, only option (d) is correctly matched.

Ethology is a branch of science dealing with study of animal behavior

subject: Science & Technology
question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Aves 1. Paleobiology B. Inheritance 2. Ecology C. Environment 3. Ornithology D. Fossils 4. Genetics Code :

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following organelles is the site of protein synthesis in a cell?
explanation: Ribosome is a complex molecule made of ribosomal RNA molecules and proteins. Ribosomes are the site of protein Synthesis. Ribosomes are associated with the plasma membrane of the cell.
source: Mizoram PSC (Pre) 2023 · General Science & Technology GS p.152

subject: Science & Technology
question: Arrange the following categories on the order of mitotic cell division. A. Prophase B. Metaphase C. Anaphase D. Telophase The correct order is
explanation: Mitosis is pair of cell cycle in which replicated chromosomes are separated into two new nuclei Mitosis consists of five Morphologically distinct phases, these are – Prophase, Prometaphase Metaphase, Anaphase and Telophase. Hence option (a) is the correct answer.
source: JKPSC (Pre) 2023 · General Science & Technology GS p.152

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which cell organ is referred to as suicide bags?
explanation: A lysosome is a membrane-bound cell organelle that contains digestive enzymes. Lysosomes are involved with various cell processes. They breakdown of various worn out cell parts of the cell, thus they help in cell cleansing. They also destroy pathogens such as bacteria and viruses and play a role in immunity. They are also called a suicidal bag of the cell because they help in self destruction of the cell.
source: Sikkim PSC (Pre) 2022 · General Science & Technology GS p.152

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following cell organelles play the most significant role in protein synthesis?
explanation: The main function of endoplasmic reticulum is to synthesize all the fats and proteins that make up various membranes, such as cell membranes, nucleus membranes, etc. Ribosome is made up of protein and RNA .The ribosome participates in protein synthesis. E.R.(Endoplasmic Reticulum) show Ribosomes attached to their outer surface. The endoplasmic Reticulum bearing ribosome on their surface is called rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER). In the absence of Ribosomes they appear smooth and called Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER).
source: IAS (Pre) GS-2001 · General Science & Technology GS p.152

subject: Science & Technology
question: The most abundant substance found in protoplasm–
explanation: The most abundant inorganic constituent of the protoplasm is the water. The entire content of a living cell is known as protoplasm. It includes the cytoplasm and the nucleus. Protoplasm is called the living substance of the cell. Water constitutes about 65 to 80% of the protoplasm. In the protoplasm, the water occurs in two forms, viz, free water and bound water. The 95% of the total cellular water is used by the protoplasm as the solvent for various inorganic substances and organic compounds and is known as free water. The remaining 5% of the total cellular water remains loosely linked with protein molecules by hydrogen bonds or other forces and is known as bound water.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · General Science & Technology GS p.152

subject: Science & Technology
question: The following cell organelle is known as 'Suicidal bags':
explanation: Lysosomes are cell organelles found in eukaryotic cells. They are also called as suicidal bags. They contain digestive enzymes and lysozymes which breaks down the waste material and foreign particles. They also destroy the cell after it has died. Lysosomes are membrane bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the golgi apparatus. The Isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all type of hydrolytic enzymes which are optimally active at the acidic pH like lipases, proteases, carbohydrates etc.
source: Nagaland NCS Prelime-2019 · General Science & Technology GS p.153

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following organelle is called 'Power House' of the cell?
explanation: Mitochondria is called the ‘power house of the cell’. The process of respiration takes place in the cytoplasm and mitochondria of each living cell and this process creates energy for cells. The ATP acts as the energy currency of the cell because of which the whole cell and body gets energy.
source: General Science & Technology GS · General Science & Technology GS p.153

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which part of the animal cell is called power house?
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S., 2010 · General Science & Technology GS p.153

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following is not present in animal cell?
explanation: Cell wall made of celluolose is not present in animal cell. The cell wall is the non-living structure of the cell made up of cellulose in plant cells. It is very tough, and rigid layer that surrounds some types of cells. It surrounds the cell membrane and provides these cells with structural support and protection. In addition, the cell wall is acting as a filtering mechanism.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S., 2010 · General Science & Technology GS p.153

subject: Science & Technology
question: Prokaryotic cells does not contain –
explanation: There are two types of cells - prokaryotic and eukaryotic. Prokaryotic cells are primitive cells, lack a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. Examples: bacteria, bacteriophages, green-blue algae etc. Whereas in eukaryotic cells, well developed cell organelles and nucleus are found. Biology
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2001 · General Science & Technology GS p.153

source: Haryana PCS (Pre) 2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.153

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which organelle in the cell, besides nucleus, contains DNA?
explanation: DNA is found in nucleus and mitochondria. DNA act to carry the genetic properties from one generation to another and control protein synthesis. Centrioles are paired barrel-shaped organelles located in the cytoplasm of animal cells near the nuclear envelope. Centrioles play a role in organizing microtubules that serve as the cell's skeletal system. Golgi apparatus is a membrane bound organelle found in most eukaryotic cells. It is responsible for packaging proteins into vesicles prior to secretion and therefore plays a key role in the secretory pathway. A lysosome is a membrane-bound cell organelle that contains digestive enzymes. Lysosomes are involved with various cell processes. They break down excess or worn-out cell parts. They may be used to destroy invading viruses and bacteria.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Energy is stored in liver and muscles in the form of:
explanation: Glycogen is a multi-branched polysaccharide of glucose that serves as a form of energy storage in animals, fungi, and bacteria. The polysaccharide structure represents the main storage form of glucose in the body. Glucose is transported by the blood to the various tissues and organs where it is used as energy. If the body does not need glucose for energy, it stores glucose in the liver and the skeletal muscles in a form called, glycogen. Glycogen stores are used as an energy source. When body needs glucose glycogen breaks into glucose and comes to blood and when blood has excess glucose, glycogen is synthesized in the liver and muscle.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.162

question: Which one of the following is NOT true about the structure of DNA?
options: DNA is a double stranded helix with sugar- phosphate as backbone.

DNA strands run in opposite direction
DNA has both major and minor grooves
explanation: About the structure of DNA , option (b) is not true because normal B-DNA, as first described by Watson and Crick, is a right-handed helix. GC-rich DNA can also exist in a form known as Z-DNA, which forms a left-handed helix. Other than this, Double-helix structure of DNA is made of two polynucleotide chains, where the backbone is constituted by sugar-phosphate. DNA molecules have an anti-parallel structure, i.e., the two strands of the helix run in opposite directions of one another. DNA has both major and minor grooves. Grooves are actually present in the structure of DNA, they serve an important role in replication and transcription.

question: The characteristics features of genetic code are i. It is always universal ii. It is triplet of nucleotides bases corresponding to 20 amino acids iii. It is non-overlapping, non-ambiguous and commaless iv. It has start and stop codon Which of the statement given above are true?
explanation: The genetic code consists of the sequence of bases in DNA or RNA. It is universal, unambiguous and redundant. Group of three bases form codon, and each codon stands for one amino acid (start or stop). The codons are read in sequence following the start codon until a stop codon is reached. The four bases of nucleotide i.e. Adenine (A), Guanine (G), Cytosine (C), and Uracil (U) are used to produce three-base codons. The 64 codons involve sense codons (that specify amino acids). Hence, there are 64 codons for 20 amino acids since every codon for one amino acid means that Triplet code exist more than code for the same amino acid.
source: MPPCS (Pre.) 2020 · General Science & Technology GS p.164

Crossing over leads to recombination of genetic material on the two chromosomes.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Double-helical structure of DNA was given by whom?
explanation: DNA stands for Deoxyribo Nucleic Acid. It was first identified in the late 1860s by Swiss chemist Friedrich Miescher. He named it "nuclein". In 1881, Albrecht Kossel identified nuclein as a nucleic acid and provided its present chemical name, Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). Between 1885 and 1901, Albrecht Kossel discovered that these acids were composed of four nitrogen bases: adenine, cytosine, guanine and thymine. He received Noble Prize for Physiology or Medicine for this work in the year 1910. Double-helix structure of DNA was propounded by James Watson and Francis Crick in the year 1953. In 1962, Watson , Crick , and Wilkins jointly received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for determination of the structure of Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).
source: UP PCS (Pre)-2018 Himachal PCS (Pre)-2018 · General Science & Technology GS p.164

This technique is used in cases when mothers carry genes for mitochondrial diseases. In Pronuclear transfer technique MRT is done after In Vitro Fertilization (IVF). Hence Statement 1 is true. subject: Science & Technology
question: In humans, trisomy of chromosome number 21 is responsible for
explanation: In humans, trisomy of chromosome number 21 is responsible for Down Syndrome. It is a genetic disorder and effected person has mental retardation. Down syndrome is known as ‘Mongolian idiocy’ . Turner syndrome, a condition that affects only females, results when one of the X chromosomes (sex chromosomes) is missing or partially missing. Turner syndrome can cause a variety of medical and developmental problems, including short height, failure of the ovaries to develop and heart defects. Klinefelter syndrome (KS) refers to a group of chromosomal disorders in which the normal male karyotype, 46,XY, has at least one extra X chromosome. XXY aneuploidy, the most common human sex chromosome disorder, has a prevalence of 1 in 500 males. Haemophilia is a rare hereditary disorder carried by females and expressed by males. Hemophilia is a disorder in which a person's blood is not able to clot normally. Down syndrome is a genetic disorder, which is caused due to changes in the number of the chromosomes. The cause of this genetic disorder is the presence of an additional copy of the chromosome number 21 (trisomy of 21). This disorder was first described by John Langdon Down (1866). The affected individual is short statured with small round head, furrowed tongue and partially open mouth. Palm is broad with characteristic palm crease. physical, psychomotor and mental development is retarded.

explanation: The reason of large-scale diversity among the organisms is Mutation. A mutation is a sudden change in a DNA sequence. Mutations can result from DNA copying mistakes made during cell division, exposure to ionizing radiation, exposure to chemicals called mutagens, or infection by viruses.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.171

subject: Science & Technology
question: Genetics deals with–
explanation: Genetics deals with heredity and variations. Those traits, transmit one generation to another, are known as hereditary traits and its study is called Genetics. Inheritance was firstly introduced by Gregor Johann Mendel, an Austrian pastor that is why he is known as father of Genetics. He used pea plant to perform his experiments. His experiments were based on concept of sexual reproduction. Double-helix structure of DNA was propounded by Watson and Crick in the year 1953. Evolution is the change in the characteristics of a species over several generations and relies on the process of natural selection. There are three theories to explain evolution as: (i) Lamarckism (ii) Darwanism (iii) Mutations
source: BPSC (Pre) 2011 · General Science & Technology GS p.171

question: Sexual reproduction causes genetic variation because of:
explanation: Sexual reproduction causes genetic variation because of blending of genes, chromosomal changes and shuffling of genes. 46 chromosomes are present in human. Every progeny receives one chromosome from female gamete and another from male gamete, in each pair of chromosomes.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2011 · General Science & Technology GS p.171

subject: Science & Technology
question: In some people only one X-Chromosome is found, this condition is called–
explanation: In some people only X-Chromosomes are found, this condition is called Turner’s syndrome. Turner syndrome, is a condition that affects only females, results when one of the X chromosomes (sex chromosomes) is missing or partially missing. Turner syndrome can cause a variety of medical and developmental problems, including short height, failure of the ovaries to develop and heart defects.This condition affects approximately 1 in 2,000 females.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Zoology Opt. 2006 · General Science & Technology GS p.171

subject: Science & Technology
question: Albinism is caused due to the deficiency of a/an:
explanation: The disease albinism is caused by the deficiency of tyrosinase enzyme. Albinism is an inherited disorder, that is characterized by little or no production of the pigment melanin, due to lack of tyrosine enzyme. This enzyme helps the body to change the amino acid tyrosine into melanin pigment. In albinism, the enzyme is inactive and no melanin is produced, leading to white hair and very light skin color.
source: OPSC (OCS) Pre 2021 Paper-I · General Science & Technology GS p.171

subject: Science & Technology
question: Genetic disorder are:
explanation: Genetic disorder are non-communicable diseases. It is caused by an abnormality in the genetic makeup of an individual. The genetic abnormality can range from minuscule to major from a discrete mutation in a single base in the DNA of a single gene to a gross chromosomal abnormality involving the addition or subtraction of an entire chromo-some or set of chromosomes.
source: OPSC (OCS) Pre-2018 · General Science & Technology GS p.171

subject: Science & Technology
question: More Men may suffer from color blindness in comparison to women, because-
options: They go through more mental stress
They stay out of the house for more time
The have only one X chromosome
explanation: Colour blindness is more common in men than in women because the genes responsible for the color blindness are located on the X chromosome. Males have only one X chromosome whereas females have two X chromosomes. In males, only one defective X chromosome is enough to cause colour blindness. In females, two defective X chromosomes are required to cause colour blindness. This type of inheritance pattern is called X-linked inheritance and it primarily affects males. 1. Consider the following events: 1. First reptiles 2. First insects 3. Shelled animals
source: BPSC (Pre) 1996 · General Science & Technology GS p.171

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following scientists is associated with the Theory of Natural Selection during evolution of life?
explanation: Charles Darwin is associated with the Theory of Natural Selection during evolution of life. The Theory of Evolution by Natural Selection, first formulated in Darwin's book " Origin of Species" in 1859, advocates the process by which organisms change over time as a result of changes in heritable physical or behavioral traits. Natural Selection is a drawn-out, complex process involving multiple interconnected causes. Natural selection requires variation in a population of organisms.
source: Himachal PCS (Pre)-2018 · General Science & Technology GS p.172

explanation: Arrangement of the species according to their chronological order of evolution is as follows : Fishes → Amphibians → Reptiles → Birds Biology 18 ORGANIC EVOLUTIO
source: UPPSC ACF (Pre) 2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.172

subject: Science & Technology
question: The modern theory of the origin of life was presented by:
explanation: The modern theory of the origin of life proposed by A.I. Oparin. Miller proved this theory through experiment. Origin of species by natural selection theory was introduced by Darwin.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Opt. Zoology, 1997 · General Science & Technology GS p.172

question: In the context of organic evolution, the loss of limbs in snakes is explained by the phenomenon of:
explanation: The loss of limbs in snakes is explained by the phenomenon of use and disuse of organs. The doctrine, proposed by the French naturalist Jean- Baptiste Lamarck in 1809.
source: IAS (Pre) GS 2002 UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.172

subject: Science & Technology
question: In which period mammals emerged–
explanation: The first mammals evolved near the end of the Triassic Period. Mammals are emerged near Triassic – Permian boundary. Indeed, Triassic period is considered as ‘Era of Reptiles’. However, first true mammals appeared in late Triassic period. The Mesozoic era is known as Golden age of reptiles. The Mesozoic era is divided in three period- (1) Triassic (2) Jurassic (3) Cretaceous Jurassic period was golden age of dinosaurs. The Cretaceous period ended with the dramatic extinction of the dinosaurs.
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2006 · General Science & Technology GS p.172

subject: Science & Technology
question: The golden age of dinosaurs was–
explanation: Mesozoic period, which spans from about 252 million years ago to about 66 million years ago, was also known as the golden age of reptiles and dinosaurs.The Mesozoic Era is divided up into the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods.During the Mesozoic, or "Middle Life" Era, life diversified rapidly and giant reptiles, dinosaurs and other monstrous beasts roamed the Earth.
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.172

explanation: The mutation theory of evolution was enunciated by Hugo de Vries. According to Mutation theory new species are formed from the sudden and unexpected emergence of alterations in their defining traits

question: Dinosaurs were in–
explanation: Dinosaurs were present in Jurassic period of Mesozoic era which time duration limits about 18 million years. The Mesozoic era is divided into the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods. Origin of toothed birds, development of giant reptiles and emergence of mammal etc took place in this era. The petrified eggs of Dinosaurs were recently found in Meerakhedi Village of West Gujarat, India.

question: Darwin's Theory of Natural Selection is based on–
explanation: Darwin's Theory of Natural Selection is based on concept of overproduction, struggle for existence and variation and survival of the fittest. Charles Darwin is associated with the theory of natural selection during evolution of life. The theory of evolution by natural selection was first formulated in Darwin's book " Origin of Species" in 1859, is the process by which organisms change over time as a result of changes in heritable physical or behavioral traits. Natural selection is a drawn-out, complex process involving multiple interconnected causes. Natural selection requires variation in a population of organisms.

subject: Science & Technology
question: The cause of evolution is-
explanation: In biology, evolution is the change in the characteristics of a species over several generations and relies on the process of natural selection. Natural selection is the only mechanism known to cause the evolution of adaptations, so many biologists would simply define an adaptation as a characteristic that has evolved by natural selection. The cause of evolution is adaptation. Adaptation is the biological mechanism by which organisms adjust to new environments or to changes in their current environment. The theory of adaptation was proposed by Charles Darwin.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2003 - 04 · General Science & Technology GS p.173

subject: Science & Technology
question: Who explained the evolution of life first?
explanation: Lamarck was biologist who explained the evolution of life first. His theory is known as Lamarckism. Lamarckism strongly builds on the notion of Internal Vital Force in organisms. From an evolutionary perspective, organs develop if it is constantly used. If unused, it could disappear. Lamarckism discredits struggle for existence.All acquired traits are transferred to the next generation.Lamarckism does not consider theory of 'survival of the fittest'. Darwin also defined evolution through natural selection while Newton & Einstein were associated mainly with Physics.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1999 · General Science & Technology GS p.173

subject: Science & Technology
question: The main factor of evolution is–
explanation: The main factor of evolution is natural selection. All organisms have ability to survive and reproduce. Natural selection works because resources are limited in nature, organisms with heritable traits that favour survival and reproduction will tend to leave more offspring than their peers, causing the traits to increase in frequency over generations. Natural selection causes populations to become adapted, or increasingly well-suited, to their environments over time. Natural selection depends on the environment and requires existing heritable variation in a group.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · General Science & Technology GS p.174

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following in human is not a Vestigial Organ?
explanation: Incisors in human is not vestigial organ. Tonsils, Nictitating Membrane, Ear lobes of External Ear, Wisdom Tooth, Coccyx, Appendix, Sinuses are are vestigial organ in human. Vestigial organs are the organs that have no apparent function and are considered to be the residual parts from the past ancestors.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2003 - 04 · General Science & Technology GS p.174

subject: Science & Technology
question: Archaeopteryx is–
options: Most ancient bird of Jurassic age
Reptile of both Triassic and Jurassic period
explanation: Archaeopteryx is most ancient bird of Jurassic age. It was the connecting link between reptiles and birds that had long tail like reptiles, toothed beak and foot bones free of the tarsometatarsus. There were giant reptiles called Dinosaurs found in this period. Dinosaurs became extinct about 66 million years ago, at a time when there was worldwide environmental change resulting from the impact of a large celestial object with the Earth and/or from vast volcanic eruptions
source: BPSC (Pre) 1995 · General Science & Technology GS p.174

subject: Science & Technology
question: Mammoth is the ancestor of–
explanation: Mammoth is the ancestor of elephant. Its scientific name is ‘Mammuthus primigenius’. Frozen woolly mammoth carcasses had been excavated from Biology 18 Tundra region of New Siberian region in 2013. The carcass contained well-preserved muscular tissue. When it was extracted from the ice, liquid blood spilled from the abdominal cavity due to its antifreezing properties.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S., 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.174

subject: Science & Technology
question: Latest ancestor of modern human is
explanation: Latest ancestor of modern human is Cro- Magnon man. These are the first early Modern Humans of the European Upper Paleolithic Age. It appeared during Holocene period that existed about 40,000 years ago. The cranial capacity was about 1,650 cc, larger than the average of modern humans. The body was generally heavy and solid with strong muscles. The face was short and wide and chin was prominent. The capacity of talking and speaking were developed more in Cro-Magnon man.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · General Science & Technology GS p.174

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following is considered the latest ancestor for of humans?
explanation: Cro-Magnon human is considered the latest ancestor of humans. The brain capacity of the Cro- magnon Man was about 1,600 cc (100 cubic inches), somewhat larger than the average for modern humans. Cro-Magnons seem to have been a settled people, moving only when necessary to find new preys or because of environmental changes.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre.) G.S. 1994-95 · General Science & Technology GS p.174
