question: What was absent at the time of origin of life on the earth?
explanation: The primitive atmosphere of earth was reducing atmosphere with no oxygen but was rich in water vapour, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, nitrogen and hydrogen. Owing to immense long lasting rainstorms, a tremendous amount of lightening was generated. Lightening provided energy for chemical reactions between hydrogen and nitrogen and carbon to form ammonia and methane.
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.175

explanation: Earth's atmosphere was reducing at the time of the origin of life because of the absence of oxygen. Only methane (CH₄) ,ammonia (NH₃) and hydrogen (H₂) were present in atmosphere at that time.

question: Smallest man-like ape is–
explanation: Smallest man-like ape is Gibbon. Gibbons are rare, small, slender, long-armed, tree-dwelling man like apes. They are arboreal, they spend most of their lives in trees. They live in old growth tropical rain forests in southeast Asia. They are part of the ape family and are classified as lesser apes because they are smaller than the great apes. The great apes are baboons, chimpanzees, gorillas, humans, and orangutans.

question: Conversion of milk into curd is done by which of the following bacteria?
explanation: Curd or Yogurt is a fermented milk product formed by fermentation of milk by Lactobacillus to Lactic acid. Milk consists of globular proteins called casein. The curd forms because of the chemical reaction between the lactic acid bacteria and casein. During fermentation, the bacteria use enzymes to produce energy (ATP) from lactose. The byproduct of ATP production is lactic acid. Lactic acid acts on the globular proteins present in the milk and denatures them.
source: ACF/RFO (Mains) IInd 2018 · General Science & Technology GS p.176

explanation: Gram positive bacteria has a single layered cell wall while in gram negative bacteria cell wall is bilayered. Cell wall of both bacteria are made up of peptidoglycan - and the bacteria remain coloured purple with Gram staining even after washing with alcohol - known as - Gram positive. The bacteria do not retain the stain when washed with alcohol known as - Gram Negative. Teichoic acid present in cell wall of Gram positive bacteria are absent in Gram Negative bacteria.

question: Assertion (A) : Some bacteria can synthesize their own food. Reason (R) : These bacteria have green matter called chloroplasts. Codes :

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

Other than this, Bacteria do not have chloroplast thus they cannot perform photosynthesis.

explanation: Medicinal mushrooms such as shiltake, reishi have been found to have antitumor and immunostimulant properties. subject: Science & Technology
question: Which is not an insect?
explanation: Spider is not an insect. Insects are a major class of the Arthropod. Spiders, Scorpions, mites and ticks come under this class of the Arachnid phylum Arthropoda. Insects come the those organisations whose body remains divided into segments. There are three pairs of legs on the chest and two pair of wings for example, house flies, Bed-bugs, mosquitoes etc. On their mouth part a pair of horns, often pair of combined eyes is also found. The reason for not keeping the spider under the insect is that the head and thorax of the spider are intert-winea. Spiders do not have wings and antennae like insects and spiders have eight legs.
source: JPSC (Pre.) 2021 Paper-I · General Science & Technology GS p.179

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following has the largest brain in proportion to its body size?
explanation: Ant has the largest brain in proportion to its body size. S.N. Species Brain:body 1. Ant 1:7 2. Human 1:40 3. Elephant 1:560
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S.-Ist 2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.179

subject: Science & Technology
question: Dolphin 1:1000 9 . Spiders are different from insects because they have–
explanation: Cockroach, Ant, Bedbug, Housefly, Mosquito, Bee and Grasshopper etc insects have six legs and four wings. Spiders are different from these insects because it has eight legs. Spiders produce seven kinds of silk (a thin, strong protein strand), ranging from sticky stuff to trap and wrap their prey to super strong threads for support. Spiders also use their silk as parachutes and to shelter themselves and their young ones Spider swallows its own web. Spiders and Scorpion both belong to phylum Arthopoda [class of Arachnida (Octapoda)].
source: RAS/RTS (Pre.) G.S. 1996 · General Science & Technology GS p.179

subject: Science & Technology
question: Lobsters belong to the class:
explanation: Lobsters belong to Crustaceans. They form a very large group of arthropods, which includes crabs, crayfish, shrimp, krill etc. Arachnids are spiders , Harvestmen mites (opiliones) and ticks.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 2009 · General Science & Technology GS p.180

subject: Science & Technology
question: How do most insects respire?
explanation: Insects breathe with a network of tiny tubes called tracheae. Most insects respire through tracheal system that lies on a network of small tubes that channel O₂ directly to the different part of the body. Respiration can occur using a variety of respiratory organs in different animals, including lungs, skin, gills, and tracheal systems . Earthworms and amphibians, such as frogs, breathe through their skin. Frog can also breath through lungs when it comes out of the water.
source: (I.A.S. Pre G.S. 2007) · General Science & Technology GS p.180

subject: Science & Technology
question: Who makes gossamer silk?
explanation: Some spiders use structures called spinnerets on the outside of their abdomens to produce the silky fiber, also known as gossamer.It is a protein fibre which is used by the spiders to make webs or other structures, which function as sticky nets to catch other animals, or as nests or cocoons to protect their offspring, or to wrap up prey.
source: UPPCS Botany Opt. 2002 · General Science & Technology GS p.180

subject: Science & Technology
question: Among the following organisms, which one does not belong to the class of other three?
explanation: Mite, scorpion and spider belong to class Arachnida while crab belongs to subphylum Crustacea. Arachnida is a group of organisms having jointed appendages.
source: (IAS (Pre) Ist Paper G.S. 2014) · General Science & Technology GS p.180

subject: Science & Technology
question: Ticks and mites are actually:
explanation: Almost all adult arachnids have eight legs. Ticks and mites are actually belong to class Arachnida in phylum Arthopoda.
source: (IAS (Pre) GS 2002) · General Science & Technology GS p.180

subject: Science & Technology
question: At which stage in its life-cycle does the silkworm yield the fiber of commerce?
explanation: Silk worm does not yield the fiber from egg and larval stage. Silk worm yield the fiber from pupa stage, which is commercially used to produce clothes. The silkworm caterpillar builds its cocoon by producing a long, continuous fiber for protection of its pupa. Raw silk is obtained from this cocoon.
source: (I.A.S. (Pre) G.S. 2000) · General Science & Technology GS p.180

subject: Science & Technology
question: Biologists have so far known, found and identified a large number of species in the plant and animal kingdom. In terms of numbers, the largest found and identified so far is from among the
explanation: In terms of numbers of species, insects certainly represent the largest percentage of the world's organisms. There are more than 1 million species of insects that have been documented and studied by scientists. The total number of documented species of living organisms at the present time is probably about 2.5 million. Insects represent about 90% of all known living species. Therefore, it is clear that, the largest found and identified number of species is of insects.
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 1996) · General Science & Technology GS p.180

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following insects is cosmopolitan?
explanation: Cosmopolitan refers to worldwide distribution. Housefly is cosmopolitan insect. The housefly is probably the insect with the widest distribution in the world. Houseflies play an important ecological role in breaking down and recycling organic matter. Their primary food is animal matter, carrion, garbage and faeces, that is why they are carriers of numerous disease. Houseflies do not serve as a secondary host or act as a reservoir of any bacteria of medical or veterinary importance, but they do serve as mechanical vectors to over 100 pathogens, such as those causing typhoid, cholera, salmonellosis, bacillary dysentery tuberculosis, anthrax, ophthalmia and pyogenic cocci.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Opt. Zoology, 1995 · General Science & Technology GS p.180

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which among the following is not an insect?
explanation: Spider belongs to class Arachnida. Spider is not an insect because insects have 6 legs and 3 main body parts (head, thorax and abdomen) while spider has 8 legs and 2 main body parts(Cephalothorax and abdomen). Insects have two pairs of wings for flying. Ants, bees, wasps, beetles, bed bugs, houseflies and weevils etc are examples of insects.
source: UPPCS Spl, (Pre) G.S. 2008 UP UDA/LDA (M) 2010 Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2010 - 11 · General Science & Technology GS p.180

subject: Science & Technology
question: In which one of the following kind of organisms is the phenomenon found wherein the female kills the male after copulation?
explanation: This phenomenon is called sexual cannibalism related to spider, in which female spider kills its mate after copulation. An interesting feature of reproduction among spiders is that many female species cannibalize their mates. Males who are eaten are smaller than the females and make an easy meal.
source: (I.A.S. (Pre) G.S. 2008) · General Science & Technology GS p.181

subject: Science & Technology
question: Glow-worm is:
explanation: Glow-worm is an insect. Glow worm gives bioluminescence in night. Class Insecta is the largest class of phylum Arthropoda. Bioluminescence is production and emission of light by living organisms.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (M) 2002 - 03 · General Science & Technology GS p.181

subject: Science & Technology
question: Termite is also called as-
explanation: Termites are also known as 'white ants'. They are small insects that eat wood and woody substances (furniture) inside the home.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (M) 2002 - 03 · General Science & Technology GS p.181

subject: Science & Technology
question: Consider the following statements about mosquitoes: 1. Only males suck blood. 2. Only females suck blood. 3. Only females suck plant sap. 4. The wings of male is larger than female. 5. The wings of female is larger than male. Among these:
explanation: Female mosquitoes have larger wings than males and only female mosquitoes suck blood, while male mosquitoes feed on fruit juice. Female mosquito required blood to produced eggs. Thus, statement 2 and 5 in the question are true. The remaining statements are false.
source: UP RO/ARO (Pre) Exam., 2016 · General Science & Technology GS p.181

subject: Science & Technology
question: Pheromones is found in-
explanation: Pheromones is found mainly in insects. Pheromone, is an endogenous chemical secreted in minute amounts by an organism in order to elicit a particular reaction from another organism of the same species. Pheromones are widespread among insects and vertebrates; they are also found in crustaceans but are unknown among birds. Pheromones are also used by some fungi, slime molds, and algae as attractants in reproduction. Pheromones play a role in sexual attraction and copulatory behaviour, and they have been shown to influence the sexual development of many mammals as well as of insects such as termites and grasshoppers. Biology 18 v. Mollusca
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S., 2008 UPPCS (Pre.) 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.181

subject: Science & Technology
question: The largest invertebrate is–
explanation: The squid of phylum Mollusca is the largest living invertebrate. Squid sometimes measures over 60 feet in length and weigh about 2 tons.Coral and Jellyfish are also marine organisms. Octopus is an invertebrate animal which may have length up to 12-14 meters. vi. Echinodermata
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. Ist Paper 2004 · General Science & Technology GS p.181

subject: Science & Technology
question: Conchology is the study of what?
explanation: Conchology is the study of mollusca shells. It is one aspect of Malacology. Malacology is the study of molluscs as a whole.
source: MH PSC (Pre) 2023 · General Science & Technology GS p.181

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: Round worm has no circulatory system
In bony fishes, swim bladder is usually present
In cartilaginous fishes, fertilisation is internal
explanation: Salient features of Echinoderms are as follow: (i) They are exclusively marine animals. (ii) The water vascular system present in echinoderms accounts for gaseous exchange, circulation of nutrients and waste elimination. (iii) They possess the power of regeneration. They reproduce sexually through gametic fusion and asexually through regeneration. (iv) Reproduction is usually external. In a very small number of species viviparous reproduction is found. (v) An excretory system is absent. Examples are Star fish, Sea urchin, Sea cucumber, Holothuria, Brittle star etc. vii. Chordata (a) Pisces
source: IAS (Pre) GS 2002 · General Science & Technology GS p.181

subject: Science & Technology
question: Insectivorous fish used for mosquito control is
explanation: Gambusia is insectivorous fish used for mosquito control. Gambusia typically eats mosquito larvae , zooplankton, beetles, mayflies, caddisflies, mites, and other invertebrates. A single carnivorous fish that can consume mosquito larvae of Anopheles is equal to its own weight each day, therefore it is useful in eradication of malaria through consuming Anopheles larvae and eggs.
source: UPPCS (Pre) GS, 2011 · General Science & Technology GS p.182

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following is a true fish?
explanation: The Exocoetus is the 'flying fish' and is in the family of marine fishes of class Actinopterygii. They are true fishes as they have streamlined body with scales and respire through gills. Flying fish can be seen jumping out of warm ocean waters worldwide. Cuttle fish are the mollusc of the order Sepiida, belonging to the class Cephalopoda e.g., squid, octopods. Silver fish or Lepisma is a small, wingless insect in the order Zygentoma. Jelly fish are major non-polyp forms in the phylum Cnidaria. Biology
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2004 · General Science & Technology GS p.182

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following is not a true fish?
explanation: Starfish popularly called sea stars are related to the phylum Echinodermata while true fishes belong to the phylum Chordata. Starfish do not have gills, scales or fins which are basic characteristics of fishes.There are some organisms which are not fishes but their names resemble to fishes, like Jelly fish, Cuttle fish, Razor fish, Silver fish, Cray Fish, Devil fish etc.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2010 - 11 · General Science & Technology GS p.182

subject: Science & Technology
question: Fish generally breath through:
explanation: Fish generally breath through gills while mammals including humans breath through lungs.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (M) 2006 · General Science & Technology GS p.182

subject: Science & Technology

explanation: Catfish is true fish while Silver fish is wingless insect. Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans resembling small lobsters while Jelly fish(Aurelia) is a coelenterate.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (M) 2002 - 03 · General Science & Technology GS p.182

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following is a true fish?

source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 1997 - 98 UP Lower (Pre) 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.182

subject: Science & Technology
question: Fishes die on putting out of water because-
options: They get excess amount of oxygen.
explanation: Fishes die on putting out of water because they can’t breathe. Fish breath with their gills, and they need a constant supply of oxygen. Fishes do not have lungs and nasal to breathe like us. Most fishes exchange dissolved oxygen and carbon dioxide in water by means of the gills.Water taken in continuously through the mouth passes backward between the gill bars and over the gill filaments, where the exchange of gases takes place. Blood moves in and out of the gills through these small blood vessels. Fish take in oxygen-rich water via their mouths and pump it over their gills. When water moves over the gill filaments, the blood within the capillary network takes up the dissolved oxygen. Then, the circulatory system supplies oxygen to all tissues of the body and finally to the cells while taking up carbon dioxide that is eliminated through the gills from the body.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · General Science & Technology GS p.182

subject: Science & Technology
question: How many bones are there in Shark fish?
explanation: Cartilaginous fishes (chondrichthyes) represent the oldest surviving jawed vertebrates and, as the name suggests, have a skeleton madeup of cartilage, but little or no bone internally . They include sharks, rays, and skates (elasmobranchii) and chimeras (holocephali).
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2010 - 11 · General Science & Technology GS p.182

question: Cold-blooded animals are:

Those whose body temperature is fixed.
Those whose body temperature varies according to the environment.
explanation: Cold-blooded animals can be defined as the animals which cannot regulate their internal body temperature with the change in the environment. They cannot survive in extreme temperature conditions. Examples of cold-blooded animals are reptiles, fish, etc. (b) Amphibia
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.183

explanation: Frog have three chambered heart. They are animals of class Amphibia.These can live both on land and in water.They are cold blooded animals.They respire through the lungs, skin and gills.The frog heart has three chambers: two atria and a single ventricle.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2013 · General Science & Technology GS p.183

subject: Science & Technology
question: Amphibians are–

explanation: Amphibians are animals that can live on land as well as in water. Eg., Frogs, Salamanders.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following animal breathe with its skin?
explanation: Frogs respire on land and in the water by two different methods in water, skin act as aquatic respiratory organ (Cutaneous respiration). Dissolved oxygen in the water is exchanged though the skin by diffusion. On Land, the buccal cavity, skin and lungs acts as respiratory organs. The respiration by Lungs is called pulmonary respiration. Frog has special characterstics of cutaneous respiration.The trait of cutaneous respiration is present in all three order of amphibians: Caudata (salamanders and newts), Anura (frogs and toads), and Caecilians (uniquely legless amphibians). Breathing through skin is known as cutaneous respiration.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre.) G.S. 2010 · General Science & Technology GS p.183

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following pairs belongs to the category of cold- blooded animals? Biology
explanation: Snake and frog belong to the category of cold blooded animals. They are known as heterotherms. Cold-blooded are the animals whose body temperature do not fluctuate with the surrounding. They are unable to maintain a constant body temperature. Mammals and birds are homeotherms, as they maintain constant body temperature. Cold blooded Animals (Poikilotherms)- There animals lack the capacity to regulate the body temperature. Ex.- Fishes, Amphibian, Reptiles. Homeotherms or warm blooded or endothermic animals:- Body temperature remain constant. Ex:- Birds, Mammals
source: UPPSC Food & Sanitary Inspector Exam. 2013 · General Science & Technology GS p.183

subject: Science & Technology
question: The only snake that builds a nest is:
explanation: The only snake that builds a nest is King Cobra. The king cobra is the only snake species that is known to make nests for their young ones.The females make a specialized nest for their eggs in 3 to 4 days in where it lays 20 to 50 eggs at a time. King cobra (Ophiophagus hannah) is the largest venomous snake in the world, found predominantly in forests in India through Southeast Asia to the Philippines and Indonesia. The King cobra's generic name, Ophiophagus is a Greek- derived word that means 'snake-eater'. Small snakes and rats are main food of King Cobra.
source: Himachal PCS(Pre)-2014 · General Science & Technology GS p.183

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following does not contain sex chromosomes?
explanation: Lizards does not contain sex chromosomes. Lizards have temperature-dependent sex determination.
source: UPPCS (Main) Spl. G.S. IInd , 2004 · General Science & Technology GS p.183

subject: Science & Technology
question: Venomous lizard is–
explanation: Heloderma is only venomous lizard in the world. There are two specieses of Heloderma namely- Heloderma suspectum (Gila monster) and Heloderma horridum (Mexican beaded lizard). Its venom is a fairly mild neurotoxin. Draco is known as flying lizard while Hemidactylus is commonlizard/wall lizard. It can shed its own tail at the time of emergency therefore it is called Autotomy-power of Regeneration is well marked.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Opt. Zoology, 1998 · General Science & Technology GS p.184

subject: Science & Technology
question: King cobra is the only snake that makes its own nest. Why does it makes nest?
options: It is a snake-eater and the nest helps attract other snakes.
It is a viviparous snake and needs a nest to give birth to its offspring.
It is oviparous snake and lays its eggs in the nest and guards the nest until they are hatched.
It is a large, cold blodded animal and needs a nest to hibernate in the cold season
explanation: King cobra is the only snake that makes its own nest for reproduction. It is oviparous snake and lays eggs in the nest and guards the nest until they are hatched.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2010 · General Science & Technology GS p.184

subject: Science & Technology
question: For which one of the following snakes takes the diet mainly composed of other snakes?
explanation: The favourite food of the King Cobra is, surprisingly other snakes. Pythons, tree snakes or other venomous species are all eaten by king cobra. Birds and mammals are also sometimes taken by this snake.
source: I.A.S. (Pre) G.S. 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.184

subject: Science & Technology
question: Haemotoxic venom which breaks Red Blood Corpuscles , is generated by which snake?
explanation: The hemolytic toxin is produced by the viper snake. Snake venom is a highly modified form of saliva, which is mainly made up of proteins and polypeptides, some toxins invade the nervous system, some to the blood and some venoms are both neurotoxic and heamotoxic.
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2009 · General Science & Technology GS p.184

subject: Science & Technology
question: Actually the venom glands of Snakes are:
explanation: The venom gland of snakes is in reality the salivary gland. It is located behind the eyes on both sides of the head and below. The toxin is produced in the venom gland itself, which is a type of biological protein. (d) Aves
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2002 · General Science & Technology GS p.184

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following is not a flightless bird?
explanation: Sarus-Crane is not a flightless bird. It is non- migratory crane found in parts of the Indian subcontinent, southeast Asia and Australia. Flightless birds are birds that have no ability to fly such as Ostriches, Emu, Kiwi and Penguins etc.
source: UK RO-ARO (Pre.) 2021 · General Science & Technology GS p.184

subject: Science & Technology
question: When flying bird starts falling due to moving around, it is prevented by -
explanation: While flying the bird starts falling due to moving around, it is prevented by spreading wings. The bird maintain equilibrium through spreading wings and this adaptation facilitates their flight.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.184

subject: Science & Technology
question: The bird that can move its upper jaw is-
explanation: Parrots can move its upper jaw. Parrot is a colourful bird that is distributed over world wide. Parrots can be found in every color of the spectrum. There are many species of parrots found in Asia as Psittacula krameri, Psittacula eupatria etc. Parrot belongs to family Psittacidae, order Psittaciformes of class Aves. It is native of the warm countries .
source: Uttarakhand RO/ARO, 2016 · General Science & Technology GS p.184

subject: Science & Technology
question: Archaeopteryx is the connecting link between which classes of organisms?
explanation: Archaeopteryx is the connecting link between class Reptilia and Aves. Archaeopteryx is known to be a connection between reptiles and birds because it looks like a bird and has bird wings. The teeth and tail, however, are closer to those of reptiles. Since it implies that birds evolved from reptiles. Therefore, Archaeopteryx links reptiles and birds.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S., 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.184

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following birds gives milk?
explanation: Pigeon is the bird in which both female and male pigeons produce milk by crop gland. Crop gland can be defined as an expanded muscular pouch near throat in the piegons. Not all birds have a crop gland. In adult pigeons, the crop glands can produce crop milk to feed newly hatched birds.
source: UPPSC Asst. Forest Conservator Exam. 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.184

subject: Science & Technology
question: The fastest running bird is-
explanation: The fastest running bird is Ostrich. Infact, ostrich is the world’s biggest bird. Ostriches are found in the wild, in deserts and savannahs of Africa. An Ostrich’s wings are small, but its legs and neck are very long. Its long, thick, and powerful legs can cover great distances without much effort, and its feet have only two toes for greater speed. Ostriches hold their wings out to help them balance when they run, especially if they suddenly change direction. Ostriches like to live in groups, which helps in defense.
source: UPPSC Asst. Forest Conservator Exam. 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.185

subject: Science & Technology
question: A tree species in Mauritius failed to reproduce because of the extinction of a fruit-eating bird. Which one of the following was that bird ?
explanation: A tree species (tambalacoque or dodo tree) in Mauritus failed to reproduce because of the extinction of a fruit-eating bird Dodo. Dodos were flightless birds, related to pigeons. They evolved on the island of Mauritius in the Indian Ocean. Dodo used the fruits of this treeas their food and spread its seeds having hard endocarp, through faeces. (e) Mammalia
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 1998) · General Science & Technology GS p.185

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following mammals lays eggs?
explanation: Egg-laying mammals are also called Monotremes. Echidnas make up four of the five living species in a group of egg-laying mammals also known as Monotremes. All of the Monotremes are found only in Australia and New Guinea.
source: UPPCS Pre 2022 · General Science & Technology GS p.185

subject: Science & Technology
question: Dolphin is an example of which class?
explanation: Dolphin is an example of Mammal. Like every mammal, dolphins are warm blooded. Unlike fish, who breathe through gills, dolphins breathe air using lungs. The Ministry of Enironment Forests declared Gangath River Dolphin as its National Aquatic Animal on 18 May, 2010.
source: UK RO-ARO (Pre.) 2021 · General Science & Technology GS p.185

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following is an egg-laying mammal ?
explanation: The vast majority of mammals give live birth to their young ones but the platypus lays eggs. Platypus have no nipples. Their milk oozes out of mammary gland duct and collects in grooves on their skin, from where the nursing babies suck it up (from tufts of fur). Biology
source: Assam PSC (CCE) Pre-2021 · General Science & Technology GS p.185

subject: Science & Technology
question: Camel uses its hump for
options: balancing the body during walking in desert sand
explanation: Camel uses its hump for storing fat. Camel is known as ‘ship of desert’ because of their ability to survive in the desert climate and also the speed they have when walking. To handle hot and arid conditions, camels have many interesting adaptations. The camel uses it as nourishment when food is scarce. A camel hump can store up to 36 kilograms of fat and sustain the camel for weeks or even months without food.
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 1993) · General Science & Technology GS p.185

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following animals stores water in the intestine ?
explanation: Camel is the animal that stores water in the intestine. Camels can go for long periods of time without water. Camel has the ability to go for a long distance without drinking water and the ability to drink large quantities of water very quickly. A typical camel can drink 200 liters (53 gallons) of water in three minutes. This water is stored in the animal’s bloodstream and intestine.
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 1994) · General Science & Technology GS p.185

subject: Science & Technology
question: Consider the following animals– 1. Sea cow 2. Seahorse 3. Sea lion Which of the above is/are mammal/mammals?
explanation: Mammal, a vertebrate animal whose young ones are nourished with milk from special mammary glands of the mother. They are found on every continent and in every ocean, and range in size from tiny bumblebee bats to enormous blue whales. Sea cow and Sea lion are mammals while Seahorse is species of marine fish. Seahorses are fascinating sea creatures native to saltwater environments from the tropics to temperate zones.
source: (IAS (Pre) Ist Paper G.S. 2013) · General Science & Technology GS p.185

subject: Science & Technology
question: Consider the following: 1. Bats 2. Bears 3. Rodents The phenomenon of hibernation can be observed in which of the above kinds of animals?
options: Hibernation cannot be observed in any of the above
explanation: The phenomenon of hibernation can be observed in bats, bears and rodents. These animals hibernate in winters due to lack of dietary substances and hibernators survive on their fat storage, stored in prior to hibernation. Hibernation is a state of minimal activity and metabolic depression in endotherms.
source: (IAS (Pre) Ist Paper G.S. 2014) · General Science & Technology GS p.185

subject: Science & Technology
question: The Panda belongs to the same family as that of:
explanation: Pandas descend from the family of Bears. Panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca)belongs to family Ursidae. Pandas are bears that are native to China, where they are considered a national treasure.
source: (IAS Pre G.S. 2009) · General Science & Technology GS p.186

subject: Science & Technology
question: In the context of Indian wild life, the flying fox is a:
explanation: In the context of Indian wild life, the flying fox is a bat. India has no less than 128 species of bats in which 33 species are found in Kerala alone.
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 2009) · General Science & Technology GS p.186

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following is monogamous?
explanation: Walrus are socially monogamous mammals. Social monogamy refers to the cohabitation of one male and one female. Seal ,wolf and deer are polygamous in nature. Monogamy occurs when one male mates with one female exculusively. The individuals are known as monogamous.
source: (IAS (Pre) GS 2002) · General Science & Technology GS p.186

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following species is the largest of the 'toothed-whales'?
explanation: Sperm whale is the largest of the 'toothed- whales'. The sperm whale is the world’s largest toothed whale. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) regards the sperm whale as being "vulnerable". Sperm whales can live 70 years or more. Sperm whales are among the most cosmopolitan species.
source: UPPCS (Pre.) Re-exam. 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.186

subject: Science & Technology
question: The biggest fish of India is-
explanation: The biggest fish in the ocean is the Rhincodon typus or whale shark of the world. Whale sharks are found in all tropical and warm-temperate seas around the world, preferring water temperatures of 68 - 77° Fahrenheit. Whale sharks grow to 18 to 32.8 feet and weight 20.6 tonnes.
source: UPPCS Spl, (Pre) G.S. 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.186

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following is a mammal?
explanation: Whales are mammals found in deep sea having 34 meters length and weigh 185 tonns. Whales are mammals because they share the characteristics of other mammals. These characteristics include being able to regulate their own body temperature (warm blooded animals), growing hair and producing milk to feed their young ones. Mother whales feed their babies milk from mammary glands and they are viviparous. Viviparous animals develop into a young animal inside the uterus of mother and it is characterstic feature of mammals. Shark :- Largest true fish Squid:- Belong to phylum Mollusca Octopus (Devil fish) :– belong to phylum Mollusca

subject: Science & Technology
question: The bear commonly performing on streets is-
explanation: The bear commonly performing on streets is Sloth bear. Sloth Bear (Melursus ursinus) inhabits tropical and sub-tropical habitats across India, Nepal, Bhutan and Sri Lanka. Sloth bears are one of 8 existing bear species in the world. They split-off from other bear species roughly 4 million years ago.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. IInd , 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.186

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following does not have a gall bladder?
explanation: Rat does not have a gall bladder. Rats are constantly eating, so the bile produced by the liver is frequently used and rarely needs to be stored. Bile helps in emulsitication of fats, i.e breaking down of the fats into very small micelles. Bile also activates enzyme lipases. bile is a combination of fluids, fat, and cholesterol. Bile helps break down fat from food in intestine. The gallbladder delivers bile into the small intestine. This allows fat-soluble vitamins and nutrients to be more easily absorbed into the bloodstream. Apart from rat, horse and deer also do not have gall bladder.
source: UPPCS (Main) Spl. G.S. IInd , 2004 · General Science & Technology GS p.186

subject: Science & Technology
question: Seal belongs to class–
explanation: Seals (Phoca Vitulina) are widely distributed mammals of order Carnivora. They are marine animals, have large flippers for floating and canine teeth for hunting. They are aggressive hunters and clutch their prey with their teeth.
source: Uttarakhand UDA (Pre) 2003 · General Science & Technology GS p.187

subject: Science & Technology
question: The only mammal capable in flying is–
explanation: Bats are the only mammals capable of flight. Bats are the flying mammals, not bird. Bats are warm blooded mammals which have fur and they nurse their babies with milk. Pteropus (flying fox) is frugivorous bat. These are true flying mammals. Ecolation sensory system (Radar system) present. Their order is chiroptera.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S., 2010 · General Science & Technology GS p.187

subject: Science & Technology
question: Dolphins are classified in–
explanation: Dolphins are classified as mammals. Mammal (class Mammalia) is called any member of the group of vertebrate animals in which the young are nourished with milk from special mammary glands of the mother. Dolphin are considered most intelligent organism after human. Although, it appears like fish but it is mammal. They have warm blood and nurse their young ones. Dolphins have more than one mate, and generally produce a single offspring.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1995 · General Science & Technology GS p.187

subject: Science & Technology
question: Warm-blooded animals are those which are able to keep their body temperature–
options: Equal to the atmospheric temperature. Biology
explanation: Warm-blooded animals are those which are able to keep their body temperature constant in every climatic condition. Warm blooded animals are also called as homeotherms. Human, goat etc are warm- blooded animals.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre.) G.S. 1996 · General Science & Technology GS p.187

subject: Science & Technology
question: Amongst the following flying organisms, which one does not belong to the class Aves?
explanation: Bat does not belong to the class Aves. Only Bats are flying mammals, not bird. Bats are warm blooded mammals as they nurse their babies with milk.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. IInd Paper 2011 · General Science & Technology GS p.187

subject: Science & Technology
question: Dogs are herbivores.
explanation: Dogs are omnivores. It consumes meat as well as other edible items.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2010 - 11 · General Science & Technology GS p.187

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following animals blood is compatible with human?
explanation: The chimpanzee and humans were originated by same ancestoral species. Indeed, since the ancestor of humans split with the common ancestor of baboon and chimpanzees between 4 million and 7 million years ago in Africa. Humans share about 99% of our DNA with chimpanzees, making them our closest living relatives. Thus, Chimpanzee blood is compatible with human. Note :- Chimpanzees and Gorillas could donate blood to humans and vice versa provided they have the same blood type.
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2004 · General Science & Technology GS p.187

subject: Science & Technology
question: The number of bones in the ear of mammals–
explanation: Ear bone, also called Auditory Ossicle, any of the three tiny bones in the middle ear of all mammals. Malleus are hammer shaped, Incus are anvil shaped, stapus are stirrup shape. Together they form a short chain that crosses the middle ear and transmits vibrations caused by sound waves from the eardrum membrane to the liquid of the inner ear.
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2007 · General Science & Technology GS p.187

subject: Science & Technology
question: In which of the following animals hooves are not found?
explanation: Hooves are hard coverings that protect the toes of many animals. Hooves are made of a protein called keratin. Hooves are more like toenails. Hooves allow animals to walk for long distances on hard surfaces without damaging their toes . Horse, cattle, deer, pigs, zebra, sheep, camel, rhinoceros, goat, cow and other animals have hooves but jackal has no hoof. HUMA i. Digestive System 1. Which of the following are not the tastes of the tongue? 1. Sweet 2. Bitter 3. Salty 4. Spicy 5. Umami 6. Sour
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S.-Ist 2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.187

subject: Science & Technology
question: Pungent Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
explanation: The tastes of our tongue are Bitter, Sour, Umami, Salty and Sweet while spicy and Pungent are not the taste of the tongue. The taste buds for sweet are on the tip of tongue.
source: 69th BPSC (Pre) 2023 · General Science & Technology GS p.188

subject: Science & Technology
question: In which organ hydrochloric acid is secreted?
explanation: The best-known component of gastric juice is hydrochloric acid, he secretory product of the parietal, or oxyntic cell. It is known that the capacity of the stomach to secrete HCl is almost linearly related to parietal cell numbers.
source: MPPSC Pre 2022 · General Science & Technology GS p.188

subject: Science & Technology
question: How is liver affected on fasting for more than 10 day?
explanation: Due to continuous diminishing of glucose affect liver on fasting more than 10 days. Liver is the largest gland of body. Liver convert excessive glucose into glycogen and it convert glycogen into glucose when not eating food during fasting.
source: UPPSC RO-ARO (Pre) 2021 · General Science & Technology GS p.188

subject: Science & Technology
question: The largest gland in human body is:
explanation: The liver is the largest gland in the human body and a necessary organ of the digestive system. It is situated on the right side of the abdomen. The liver is split into a larger anatomical right lobe and a smaller anatomical left lobe which is separated by the falciform ligament.
source: NAGALAND NCS PRE-2018 · General Science & Technology GS p.188

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following human teeth shows the permanent tooth arrangement system?
explanation: Molar teeth shows the permanent tooth arrangement system. There are 12 molars in the permanent dentition with three in each quadrant of the mouth. They are named starting with closest to the midline as first molars, second molars and third molars. Although, some people do not fully develop the third molars. Third molars are often referred to as wisdom teeth. The primary dentition only contains eight molars.
source: UPPSC Asst. Forest Conservator Exam. 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.188

subject: Science & Technology
question: In human intestine, beneficial parasite protozoa present is–
explanation: E. coli is a beneficial parasite found in the large intestine of humans, it receives essential nutrients from the human body for reproduction and development. Most E. Coli strains are harmless, but some can cause serious food poisoning.
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2009 · General Science & Technology GS p.188

subject: Science & Technology
question: 'Epiglottis' in our body is a part of which system?
explanation: Epiglottis is a part of digestive system. The epiglottis is a flexible flap at the superior end of the larynx in the throat. It acts as a switch between the larynx and oesophagus to permit air to enter the airway to the lungs and prevents food and drink from entering into windpipe.
source: Nagaland PSC (NCS) Pre-2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.188

subject: Science & Technology
question: Digestion of Lipids takes place in the presence of some of the following: 1. Bile acids 2. Lipases 3. Pepsin of these:
explanation: Bile acids and Lipases play a key role in the digestion of lipids. Bile juice emulsifies fat in the duodenum while lipase converts fat into fatty acid and glycerol. Pepsin is a protein digestive enzyme.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. IInd Paper, 2016 · General Science & Technology GS p.189

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following processes in the bodies of living organisms is a digestive process?
options: Breakdown of proteins into amino acids
Breakdown of glucose into CO₂ and H₂ O
Conversion of amino acids into proteins
explanation: The transformation of complex molecules into simple molecules is called 'digestion'. Breakdown of proteins (complex molecules) into amino-acids (simple molecules) - similarly, dissolution of glucose into CO₂ and H₂ O - respiration process, conversion of glucose into glycogen - synthesis process, conversion of amino acids into proteins. As soon as the food reaches the pancreas, first of all, bile juice comes out of the liver. Bile juice is alkaline and makes the food acidic to alkaline. Here food gets pancreatic juice which is releases from pancreas, the pancreatic juice contains mainly three types enzymes which are - Trypsin - It converts proteins and peptones into polypeptides and amino acids. Amylase - It converts starch into soluble sugars. Lipase - It converts emulsified fats into glycerin and fatty acids.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2010 · General Science & Technology GS p.189

subject: Science & Technology
question: In the human body, Appendix is attached to which of the following structure?
explanation: Large intestine (larger in diameter) is differenciated into three part cecum, colon and rectum. Cecum is small blind sac which hosts some symbiotic micro organism. A Narrow finger like tubular projection, the vermiform appendix which is vestigial organ, arises from the cecum. Cecum opens into the colon. The colon is divided into four parts an ascending, transverse desending part and a sigmoid colon. The desending part opens into the rectum which opens out through the anus.
source: I.A.S. (Pre) G.S. 2007 · General Science & Technology GS p.189

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following is the hardest part of our body?
explanation: The hardest part of our body is the enamel found over the teeth. It is mainly made up of calcium phosphate and calcium carbonate. Dentin or dentine is a layer of material that lies immediately underneath the enamel of the tooth. It is one of the four major components of the tooth.
source: Uttarakhand UDA (Pre) 2003 · General Science & Technology GS p.189

subject: Science & Technology
question: Consider the following statements with reference to human body : 1. The common bile duct release its contents into stomach 2. The pancreatic duct releases its contents into duodenum Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
explanation: Bile duct and pancreatic duct both releases its contents into duodenum. The digestive enzyme (pancreatic juices) are released to duodenum from pancreatic duct. The digestive role of the liver is to produce bile and export it to the duodenum. The gallbladder primarily stores, concentrates, and releases bile. The pancreas produces pancreatic juice, which contains digestive enzymes and bicarbonate ions, and delivers it to the duodenum.
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 2006) · General Science & Technology GS p.189

subject: Science & Technology
question: With reference to normal human beings, consider the following statements– 1 . In response to the presence of HCl, secretin is produced from the duodenum. 2 . Enterogastrone is produced in the small intestine in response to the presence of fatty acids Which of these statements is/are correct?
explanation: After mouth, food passes through esophagus and reaches the stomach. After the food reaches the stomach, HCl combines with food, neutralizes the Ptyalin and makes the food acidic. From the stomach, the chyme reaches the duodenum. Here, firstly, bile juice is released from the liver. Pancreatic juices also come here and meet chyme. As a response to HCl presence, Secretin is produced from the duodenum. Enterogastron is produced in the ejaculate as a response to the presence of fatty acids.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2003 · General Science & Technology GS p.189

subject: Science & Technology
question: The main cause of tooth decay is bacteria inside the mouth and-
explanation: The main cause of tooth decay is the interactions between bacteria and particles of carbohydrates trapped between teeth.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2004-05 · General Science & Technology GS p.190

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following organs is vestigial in human body?
explanation: Vestigial organs are organs, tissues or cell in a body which are no more functional the way they were ancestral form of trait in human body. Appendix is vestigial organ but it involves in digestion of cellulose in herbivores.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Opt. Zoology, 1995 · General Science & Technology GS p.190

subject: Science & Technology
question: The number of teeth that are developed twice in the lifetime of human being is:
explanation: Majority of mammals including human being forms two sets of teeth during their life, a set of temporary, milk or deciduous teeth replaced by a set of permanent or adult teeth. An adult human has 32 permanent teeth, which are of four different types, namely, incisors (I), canine (C), premolars (PM) and molars(M). Arrangement of teeth in each half of the upper and lower jaw in the order I, C, PM, M is represented by a dental formula which in human is 2123/ 2123 which indicate 2 Incisors, 1 Canine, 2 Premolar and 3 Molars. The premolars and last molars are absent in children. Thus the teeth which grow twice are incisors, canines and two molars i.e., a total of 20 teeth. In mammals, except premolar and last molar, all type of teeth appears twice in life. Teeth which appears during childhood are called milk teeth/ lacteal teeth/ decioduous teeth/ primary teeth. Biology
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · General Science & Technology GS p.190

subject: Science & Technology
question: In the buccal cavity of human being digestion of which one of the following get started ?
explanation: , In human anatomy, mouth is also called oral cavity or buccal cavity. The buccal cavity mainly comprises the primary organ of the digestive system including the teeth, tongue and salivary glands. Digestion starts in the buccal cavity of the mouth and ends at the anus. In between, it passes through a long alimentary canal which is further divided into various components. In the buccal cavity of human being, digestion of carbohydrates get started. Saliva releases an enzyme called amylase, which breaks down starch into smaller carbohydrates.
source: MPPSC (Pre) 2019 · General Science & Technology GS p.190

subject: Science & Technology
question: Acid present in the gastric juice is
explanation: Hydrochloric acid is present in gastric juice. In fact, Gastric Juice is a unique combination of hydrochloric acid, lipase and pepsin. Acidic gastric juice is found in all vertebrates and its main function is to inactive microorganisms.

question: Assertion (A) : In human body, the liver has an important role in fat digestion. Reason (R) : Liver produces two important fat- digesting enzymes. Code :

The enzyme Ptyalin is produced by human slavery gland which hydrolyzes starch. The enzyme Pepsin protease and Trypsin is produced by Pancreas which helps in digestion of protein.

explanation: Ileum-Jejunum-Duodenum is the correct sequence in the order decreasing the length of the three structural part of the small intestine in the human body. The length of Ileum is 150 to 160 cms, Jejunum 100 to 110 cms while length of Duodenum is 20 cms. Biology

subject: Science & Technology
question: Assertion (A) : All the proteins in our food are digested in small intestine only. Reason (R) : The protein-digesting enzyme from the pancreas are released into the small intestine. Code:
options: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are individually true, but R is not a correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
explanation: Pancreas secretes pancreatic juice in which Trypsin digests protein. Erypsin, secreted by small intestine, converts all proteins in amino acids. Thus, assertion (A) is false, but reason (R) is true.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following hormone stimulates the pancreas to produce digestive juices?
explanation: Secretin is the hormone that stimulates the pancreas to produce digestive juices. Renin, enzyme secreted by the kidneys that regulates blood pressure while trypsin and pepsin digest protein during digestion.

question: In human body most of the digestive process takes place in–
explanation: In human body most of the digestive process takes place in small intestine because the bile, Pancreatic juice and the intestinal juice are secreted into small intestine.
source: UPPCS (Pre.) G.S. 1991 UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2010 · General Science & Technology GS p.191

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which organ is commonly affected by aflatoxins food poisoning in humans?
explanation: Liver is commonly affected by Aflatoxins food poisoning in humans. Aflatoxins are a family of toxins produced by certain fungi for example Aspergillus flavus and Aspergillus parasiticus.

subject: Science & Technology
question: The saliva helps in the digestion of–
explanation: The saliva helps in the digestion of starch. Saliva contains special enzymes that help digest the starches in food. An enzyme called amylase breaks down starches (complex carbohydrates) into sugars, which body can more easily absorb. Saliva also contains an enzyme called lingual lipase, which breaks down fats.

explanation: The Krebs cycle is a part of cellular respiration which comprises a series of chemical reactions used by all aerobic organism in their energy conversion processes. It produces the maximum atomic molecules in our body.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following about bile juice is incorrect?

The salt present in it emulsifies fat.
The enzymes present in it digest the fat.
explanation: Hepatocytes cells of the liver produces bile juice and it is stored in the gallbladder. Bile juice does not contain any type of digestive enzyme, it is not called true digestive, the composition of bile juice are:- Bile pigment, cholesterol, lecithin inorganic constituent Na⁺ , K⁺ etc. pH = 7.4 to 7.6 i.e. basic in nature Bile pigments are the excretory substance of the liver.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Extra glucose in body gets converted into glycogen and is stored in–
explanation: Extra glucose in body gets converted into glycogen and is stored in liver. The liver maintains normal blood glucose level. It also detoxify substances such as alcohol and excrete drugs such as penicillin, erythromycin and sulphonamides into bile.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. Ist Paper 2004 · General Science & Technology GS p.192

subject: Science & Technology
question: The stones present in the human gallbladder primarily affect the digestion of______.
explanation: The stones present in the human gallbladder primarily affect the digestion of fats. Liver is the largest gland as well as largest organ (internal) in human body. Bile is a unique and vital aqueous secretion of the liver and stored in the gallbladder. Bile contains bile salt, which are critical for digestion and absorption of fats and fat-soluble vitamins in the small intestine. Bile is alkaline in nature and helpful in emulsification of fats.

question: Human heart is made up of how many chambers?
explanation: The Human heart consists of 4 chambers namely left atrium and right atrium (Upper chambers) and the left ventricle and the right ventricle (lower chambers).

question: Which of the following is a vital role played by the mitral and the tricuspid valves of the heart?

Allowing supply of oxygenated blood to the heart
Preventing blood from flowing back into the atria

question: Consider the below two statements : Statement I : The thymus is a lobed organ located near the heart and beneath the breast bone. Statement I is correct but Statement II is false

subject: Science & Technology
question: Consider the following statements : A. Circadian rhythm is endogenous rhythmic change in organism with a periodicity of 24 hours. B. Biological clock regulates circadian rhythm. C. explanation: Circadian rhythms are the physical mental and behavioral changes an organism experiences over a 24 hour cycle. For e.g. Sleep and a wake cycle. Normal altitudes where atmospheric pressure is high

question: When does heart take rest?
explanation: Heart takes rest between two beats. When the heart beats, it pumps blood to lungs and the rest of body. But in between beats, the heart muscle relaxes as it fills with blood. It relaxes only for a moment after each contraction, but that still counts as resting.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2004 UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2009 · General Science & Technology GS p.195

subject: Science & Technology
question: The percentage of water in plasma is–
explanation: Plasma is the clear, straw- coloured liquid portion of blood that remains after red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets and other cellular components are removed. It is the single largest component of human blood. It makes up about 55 to 65% of the blood. It contains 90 to 92% water and remaining 10% to 8% of it has salts, enzymes, antibodies and other proteins.
source: UPPCS Zoology Opt. 2009 · General Science & Technology GS p.195

subject: Science & Technology
question: What is the name of the vessel that delivers the nutrient rich blood from the stomach & small intestine to the liver ?
explanation: A unique vascular connection exists between the digestive tract and liver called Hepatic Portal System. The hepatic portal vein carries blood from intestine to the liver before it is delivered to the systematic circulation.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2006 · General Science & Technology GS p.196

question: Mother-fetus Rh blood type incapability problems can occur if the mother is ...... and her fetus is.....
explanation: Rh incompatibility is a condition that develops when a pregnant woman has Rh-negative blood and her fetus is Rh positive. Rh factor is a group of antigens that determined the blood group of human beings. It was discovered by Landsteiner and Wiener.

question: What is considered to be the ideal human heartbeat rate per minute?
explanation: A normal resting heart rate for adults ranges from 60 to 100 beats per minute. Generally, a lower heart rate at rest implies more efficient heart function and better cardiovascular fitness.
source: Nagaland PSC (NCS) Pre-2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.196

subject: Science & Technology
question: The blood glucose level is commonly expressed as:
explanation: Blood glucose level expressed in two units (i) Molar concentration (ii) Mass concentration (i) In molar concentration, it is measured in mmol/L (millimoles perlitre, or millimolar (mM). (ii) In mass concentration, it is measured in mg/de (milligrams per deciliter). • Molar concentration is international standard way of measuring of blood glucose level. The blood concentration of glucose in a normal healthy individual is 3.9 m mol/L - 5.6 mmol/L.
source: UPPSC PRE 2021 IAS GS - 2000 · General Science & Technology GS p.196

subject: Science & Technology
question: What is the average lifespan of RBC?
explanation: Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to all of the cells in a living body. Blood cells also fight infection and control bleeding. Red Blood Cells (RBC), one of the most important components of blood has a life span of about 120 days. Red blood cells make up almost half of blood of a human body and are made in the bone marrow. Note- The lifespan of white blood cells in the lymph system is 13 to 20 days after which they are destroyed in the lymphatic system.
source: NAGALAND NCS PRE-2018 · General Science & Technology GS p.196

question: Why do ventricles have thicker muscular walls than atria?
options: Ventricles receive oxygen-rich blood than atria
Ventricles have to pump blood into various organs.
Atria have to pump blood into various organs.
Ventricles first receives blood from the various organs.
explanation: The ventricles of the heart have thicker muscular walls than the atria. This is because blood is pumped out of the heart at greater pressure from these chambers compared to the atria.

It is a cardiovascular disease, which is mainly caused due to the narrowed or blocked artery, which is formed due to the build of plaqueness along the walls of the arteries. Abnormal high blood pressure and a combination of high psychological stress are known as Hypertension.

Such individuals are called Rh positive (Rh+ve) and those in whom this antigen is absent are called Rh Negative (Rh–ve). An Rh (–ve) person, if exposed to Rh+ve blood, will form specific antibodies against the Rh antigens. Therefore, Rh group should also be matched before transfusions. question: An antigen is a substance which–
options: Is used as an antidote to poison.
explanation: An antigen is any substance that causes your immune system to produce antibodies against it. It is a substance which triggers the immune system. It is capable of stimulating an immune response, specifically activating lymphocytes, which are the body’s infection-fighting white blood cells. An antigen that induces an immune response—i.e., stimulates the lymphocytes to produce antibody or to attack the antigen directly—is called an Immunogen.

explanation: Blood pressure is a measurement of the force on the walls of arteries as heart pumps blood through body. The blood pressure reading is measured in millimeters of mercury (mmHg) and is written as Systolic Pressure, the force of the blood against the artery walls as heart beats, over diastolic pressure, the blood pressure between heartbeats. Blood pressure reading for normal adult is 120/80 mmHg, or "120 over 80". The systolic pressure is 120 and the diastolic pressure is 80. In given options, Mr.Y has normal blood pressure.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following physiological process is associated with Thrombin?
explanation: Thrombin is associated with physiological process ‘blood clotting’. Thrombin is a unique molecule that functions both as a procoagulant and anticoagulant. Prothrombin is transformed into thrombin by a clotting factor known as factor X or prothrombinase; thrombin then acts to transform fibrinogen, also present in plasma, into fibrin, which, in combination with platelets from the blood, forms a clot (a process called coagulation),i.e., Thrombin + Prothrombin + Calcium = Thrombin Thrombin + Fibrinogen = Fibrin Fibrin + Blood corpuscles = Blood clot
source: UPPCS (Pre) GS, 2011 UPPCS (Pre) Opt. Zoology, 2004 · General Science & Technology GS p.199

question: Which of the following is related to scarcity of blood?
explanation: Low blood pressure is related to scarcity of blood. Hypotension is the medical term for low blood pressure (less than 90/60). It is caused due to insufficient blood flow and oxygen scarcity in the brain. When the flow of blood is too low to deliver enough oxygen and nutrients to vital organs such as the brain, heart, and kidney, the organs do not function normally and may be temporarily or permanently damaged. Lack of haemoglogin and iron content causes Anaemia. Accumulation of lactic acid causes joint pain.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2001 · General Science & Technology GS p.199

subject: Science & Technology
question: Consider the following statements are correct about hemoglobin: 1 . It contains iron. 2 . It carries oxygen in the blood. 3 . It imparts red colour to the blood. 4 . It provides immunity against certain diseases The correct statements out of these are:
explanation: Hemoglobin has a critical role in human body. Hemoglobin is protein as well as respiratory pigment in red blood cells that is made up of four chains. Each of these chains contains a compound known as hemes, which in turn contains iron, which transports oxygen in the bloodstream. Hemoglobin functions by binding and transporting oxygen from the capillaries in the lungs to all the tissues in the body. It also plays a role in the transport of carbon dioxide from the tissues of the body back to the lungs. The pigment in hemoglobin is responsible for the red color of blood. The white blood cells(WBCs) or leukocytes help provide immunity by destroying or killing foreign pathogens and antigen and thereby provide protection from diseases and infections. They are therefore called as the soldiers of our body.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2001, 2003, 2005, 2016 UPPCS (Main) Spl. G.S. IInd 2004 UPPSC ACF (Pre) 2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.199

explanation: When the concentration of oxygen in the blood decreases, the speed of breathing increases. During exercise there is an increase in physical activity and muscle cells respire more than they do when the body is at rest. The heart rate increases during exercise. subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following forms irreversible synthesis in haemoglobin of blood?
options: Carbon di-oxide and mixture of Helium
explanation: Carbon monoxide forms irreversible synthesis in hemoglobin of blood. Carbon monoxide has a greater affinity for hemoglobin than oxygen. Therefore, when carbon monoxide is present, it binds to hemoglobin preferentially over oxygen. As a result, oxygen cannot bind to hemoglobin, so very little oxygen is transported through the body. Carbon monoxide is a colourless, odourless gas and is therefore difficult to detect. It is produced by gas- powered vehicles and tools. Carbon monoxide can cause headache, suffocation, and nausea; long-term exposure can cause brain damage or death. Carbon monoxide is main air pollutant that gets dissolved in hemoglobin of the blood more rapidly than oxygen.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1996 UPPCS (Pre) Zoology Opt. 2007 · General Science & Technology GS p.200

Radio-Iodine, or RA(I-131), is given as a pill, to treat hyperthyroidism by gradually shrinking thyroid— ultimately destroying the gland. Radioactive Iron is used to detect anaemia.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following minerals is necessary to control heartbeat?
explanation: Potassium is necessary mineral to control heartbeat and regulate nervous system. It is a type of electrolyte. It helps nerves to function and muscles to contract. It helps your heartbeat stay regular. It also helps move nutrients into cells and waste products out of cells. Sources of potassium in the diet include meat, fish, leafy greens, such as spinach and collards, fruits, such as grapes and blackberries, root vegetables, such as carrots and potatoes and citrus fruits, such as oranges and grapefruits.

explanation: Formation of WBC and destruction of RBC takes place in Spleen. Red blood cells, most white blood cells, and platelets are produced in the bone marrow, the soft fatty tissue inside bone cavities. Two types of white blood cells, T and B cells (lymphocytes), are also produced in the lymph nodes and spleen, and T cells are produced and mature in the thymus gland while red blood cells are destroyed in the liver or spleen.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following is referred to as the “Graveyard of RBC’s” ?
explanation: The spleen plays an important role in the red blood cells also known as erythrocytes and also in the digestive system. Old and damaged RBC's are destroyed in the spleen and it is known as the RBC's Graveyard. The spleen recycles the old and damaged red blood cells and also stores red blood cells, platelets, and infection-fighting white blood cells. The spleen plays an important role in immune system response. The average red cell in humans lives 100–120 days(4 months); there are some 5.2 million red cells per cubic millimetre of blood in the adult human.

explanation: Red Blood Corpuscles are formed mainly in the bone marrow and are believed to have an average life span of approximately 120 days. Stem cells in the bone marrow are called Hemocytoblasts. They give rise to all of the formed elements in blood. Red blood cells contain a protein called hemoglobin, which carries oxygen from the lungs to all parts of the body.

explanation: The abnormal level of cholesterol is related to hardening of arteries. The main risk associated with high cholesterol is Coronary Heart Disease (CHD). Blood cholesterol level has a lot to do with chances of getting heart disease. If cholesterol is too high, it builds up on the walls of arteries. Over time, this buildup is known as Atherosclerosis. This condition causes arteries to become narrowed, and the narrowed blood vessels reduce blood flow to the heart.

subject: Science & Technology
question: What is the function of blood in the body?
explanation: Blood is a fluid connective tissue present in human. It has four main components: plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Blood has many different functions, including transporting oxygen and nutrients to the lungs and tissues, forming blood clots to prevent excess blood loss, carrying cells and antibodies that fight infection bringing waste products to the kidneys and liver, which filter , clean the blood and regulate body temperature.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S., 2010 · General Science & Technology GS p.202

subject: Science & Technology
question: How many chambers are there in heart?
explanation: The heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles. Blood enters the right atrium and passes through the right ventricle. The right ventricle pumps the blood to the lungs where it becomes oxygenated. The oxygenated blood is brought back to the heart by the pulmonary veins which enter the left atrium. From the left atrium blood flows into the left ventricle. The left ventricle pumps the blood to the aorta which will distribute the oxygenated blood to all parts of the body.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S., 2010 · General Science & Technology GS p.202

explanation: Blood has a normal pH range of 7.35 to 7.45. Human life requires a tightly controlled pH level in the serum of about 7.4 (a slightly alkaline range of 7.35 to 7.45) to survive. Although the pH of blood ranges from 7.35-7.45, the pH of other₊ body fluids is different. pH indicates the₊ level of H ions, where low pH indicates too many H ions and high pH indicates too many OH – ions. If the pH level drops below 6.9, it can lead to coma. However, different body fluids have different pH values such as the pH of saliva is ranges from 6.5 to 7.5.

question: Red Blood Cells are formed in which part of our body?
explanation: The red cell develops in bone marrow in several stages . subject: Science & Technology
question: Heme is important biologically in the myoglobin which is used to store :
explanation: Myoglobin contains a heme (prosthetic) group which is responsible for its main function (carrying of oxygen molecules to muscle tissues). Myoglobin and hemoglobin are hemeproteins whose physiological importance is principally related to their ability to bind molecular oxygen. Functionally, myoglobin is well accepted as an O₂ -storage protein in muscle, capable of releasing O₂ during periods of hypoxia or anoxia. Myoglobin is also thought to buffer intracellular O₂ concentration when muscle activity increases and to facilitate intracellular O₂ diffusion by providing a parallel path that augments simple diffusion of dissolved O₂ .

question: What is haemoglobin?
options: A substance found in leaves of the plants
A substance found in bone marrow
A substance found in human blood
explanation: Haemoglobin is iron-containing protein in the blood of many animals—in the red blood cells (erythrocytes) of vertebrates—that transports oxygen to the tissues. It is a respiratory pigment and helps in transporting oxygen as oxyhaemoglobin from the lungs to different parts of the body. Some amount of carbon dioxide is also transported back via haemoglobin as carbaminohaemoglobin. Deficiency of hemoglobin causes Anaemia.
source: RAS/RTS(Pre.) G.S. 1992 · General Science & Technology GS p.205

subject: Science & Technology
question: Immunity is mostly related to-
explanation: Immunity is mostly related to Lymphocytes. The Immune system is a complex network of cells (such as lymphocytes) and organs that work together to defend the body against foreign substances (antigens) such as bacteria, a virus or tumor cell. When the body discovers such a substance several kinds of cells go into action in what is called an immune response. Lymphocytes are one of the main types of immune cells. Lymphocytes are divided mainly into B and T cells. B lymphocytes produce antibodies - proteins (gamma globulins) that recognize foreign substances (antigen) and attach themselves to them. T lymphocytes are cells that are programmed to recognize, respond to and remember antigens. Biology
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 1993 · General Science & Technology GS p.205

subject: Science & Technology
question: The immune protein which protects the cells from viral infection is _______.
explanation: The immune protein that protects cells from viral infection is interferon. When the body's cells are attacked by a viral infection, the cells produce an antiviral protein called interferon in response. Interferons are released from infected and dying host cells. Interferon makes living cells resistant to virus infection. Fever increases the production of interferon. In humans, there are three groups of interferons- (1) α- interferons from white blood cells (2) β - interferons from connective tissue fibroblasts (3) γ-Interferons from lymphocytes.
source: UPPSC ACF Mains 2021 Paper-II · General Science & Technology GS p.205

subject: Science & Technology
question: Antibodies are_____.
explanation: Antibodies are proteins found in the globulin fractions of blood. It recognizes foreign substances like bacteria and viruses, and neutralizes them. Antibodies are protective glycoprotein molecule formed within the body of an animal in order to neutralize the effect of a foreign invading protein (antigens). An antibody (Ab), also known as an Immunoglobulin (Ig), recognizes a unique molecule of the pathogen, called an Antigen. Antibodies are produced by specialized white blood cells called B lymphocytes (or B cells). When an antigen binds to the B-Cell surface, it stimulates the B cell to 'divide and mature into a group of identical cells called a Clone.
source: ACF/RFO (Mains) IInd 2018 · General Science & Technology GS p.205

subject: Science & Technology
question: In coronary artery bypass surgery, the blood vessel to be used as graft has to be–
options: Artery from mammary region of chest
explanation: Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Surgery (CABG) is a procedure used to treat coronary artery disease. Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is the narrowing of the coronary arteries – the blood vessels that supply oxygen and nutrients to the heart muscle. CAD is caused by build-up of a fatty material within the walls of the arteries. This build-up narrows the inside of the arteries, limiting the supply of oxygen- rich blood to the heart muscle. One way to treat the blocked or narrowed arteries is to bypass the blocked portion of the coronary artery with a piece of a healthy blood vessel from elsewhere in body. Blood vessels, or Biology 21 grafts, used for the bypass procedure may be pieces of a vein from leg or an artery in chest. An artery from wrist may also be used. Doctor attaches one end of the graft above the blockage and the other end below the blockage. Blood bypasses the blockage by going through the new graft to reach the heart muscle. This is called Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery.
source: UPPCS (Pre) GS, 2014 · General Science & Technology GS p.206

question: Which of the following is not a reflex action?
explanation: Movement of hand is not a reflex action. Sudden response to a stimulus, without the intervention of the brain, is called Reflex Action. These actions are automatic actions that occur without the will of the organism. All reflex actions are controlled by the spinal cord. The actions over which we have control are called Voluntary Actions such as speaking, walking, moving hands etc. The actions that we have no control over are called Involuntary Actions, such as beating of the heart, breathing, digesting food etc. Involuntary actions are controlled by the mid-brain and hind- brain.

Reflex action is the result of the coordination of the spinal cord and peripheral nervous system. This action does not involve the brain.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Myopia is the disorder of which organ?
explanation: Myopia is the disorder of eye. There are two types of eye defects : (i) Myopia (ii) Hyperopia/ Hypermetropia (i) Myopia is the term used to define being shortsighted. A myopic person has clear vision when looking at objects close to him, but distant objects will appear blurred. This is because light is focused in front of the retina and, being too far forward in the eye, things in the distance look blurred. Shortsightedness is corrected using a concave (curved inwards) lens which is placed in front of a myopic eye, moving the image back to the retina and making it clearer. (ii) Hypermetropia is sometimes called hyperopia, is the term used to define being farsighted. If person is hypermetropic, the image of a nearby object is formed behind the retina. This means that light is focused too far back in the eye, causing things which are close up to appear blurred. Longsightedness is corrected using a convex (outward facing) lens. This is placed in front of a hypermetropic eye, moving the image forward and focusing it correctly on the retina.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. Ist Paper, 2016 · General Science & Technology GS p.211
