subject: Science & Technology
question: Byssinosis disease is common in the workers of:
explanation: Byssinosis disease is common in the workers of textile industry. Byssinosis is a disease of the lungs. It is caused by breathing in cotton dust or dusts from other vegetable fibers such as flax, hemp, or sisal while at work. It causes asthma-like breathing difficulty. People with byssinosis usually have a cough and feelings of chest tightness. Long-term exposure can cause disability but rarely death.
source: UPSC CAPF Exam. Ist 2012 · General Science & Technology GS p.285

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following disease is caused by the excessive use of alcoholic beverage?
explanation: Liver cirrhosis disease is caused by the excessive use of alcoholic beverage. Alcohol- related liver disease (ARLD) is caused by damage to the liver from years of excessive drinking. Years of alcohol abuse can cause the liver to become inflamed and swollen. This damage also cause scarring known as cirrhosis. Cirrhosis is the final stage of liver disease.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. IInd , 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.285

subject: Science & Technology
question: Sleep apnea is a serious sleep disorder, in which people –
options: walk during sleep without knowing what he or she is doing.
briefly and repeatedly stop breathing during sleep.
make loud snoring sound while sleep.
explanation: Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which person pause in breathing during sleep. Each pause can last for a few second to a few minutes and they happen many times a night.
source: UPPCS (Pre) GS, 2014 · General Science & Technology GS p.285

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following cannot be the cause of dangerous "dropsy" occurring in people eating adulterated mustard oil cooked food (as happened in India) –
explanation: Oil adulteration of paddy husk cannot be the cause of dangerous "dropsy" occurring in people eating adulterated mustard oil cooked food (as happened in India). Argemone toxicity causes the disease called epidemic dropsy and is characterized by pathological accumulation of diluted lymph in body tissues and cavities. It contains Cyanide and it is fatal. Biology
source: UP Lower (Pre) 1998 · General Science & Technology GS p.285

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following dust components cause problems for asthma patients?
explanation: Asthma is an element which is marked with difficulty in breathing causing wheezing due to inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles. Inorganic particle and pollen grain cause problems for asthma patients. Bronchial asthma is an inflammatory disease of the airways which may be worsened due to numerous extrinsic factors. The most common trigger is continuous exposure to allergens of which fungal agents (Aspergillus fungitus) are important factors. It is not contagious disease.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (M) 2004-05 · General Science & Technology GS p.285

subject: Science & Technology
question: Phenylketonuria is an example of an inborn error of metabolism. This “error” refers to:
explanation: Phenylketonuria is an example of an inborn error of metabolism. This “error” refers to inherited lack of an enzyme. Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an autosomal recessive inborn error of phenylalanine (Phe) metabolism resulting from deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH). Most forms of PKU and hyperphenylalaninaemia (HPA) are caused by mutations in the PAH gene on chromosome. Untreated PKU is associated with an abnormal phenotype which includes growth failure, poor skin pigmentation, microcephaly, seizures, global developmental delay and severe intellectual impairment.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1994 · General Science & Technology GS p.285

subject: Science & Technology
question: Three communicable diseases prevalent in developing countries caused by unsafe drinking water and bad sanitation are:
explanation: Three communicable diseases prevalent in developing countries caused by unsafe drinking water and bad sanitation are malaria, acute diarrhoea and schistosomiasis. Cholera, Jaundice and Typhoid are the diseases that are also transmitted through contaminated water and food. Cancer is caused by uncontrolled abnormal growth of cancer cells, AIDS is spread through unprotected sex, infected blood and injections.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1993 · General Science & Technology GS p.285

subject: Science & Technology
question: Scratching eases itching because
options: it removes the outer dust in the skin.
it stimulates certain nerves which direct the brain to increase the production of antihistaminic chemicals.
it suppresses the production of enzymes which cause itching.
explanation: Scratching eases itching because it stimulates certain nerves which direct the brain to increase the production of antihistaminic chemicals.
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 1993) · General Science & Technology GS p.286

subject: Science & Technology
question: When doctor tells a person that he/she has been affected with tetraplagia, it means that he/she is suffering from paralysis of_______.
explanation: When doctor tells a person that he/she has been affected with tetraplagia, it means that he/she is suffering from paralysis of both hands and both legs. Tetraplegia is a paralysis caused by an injury of the cervical spinal cord. This can result in a partial or total sensory and motor loss of the four limbs and torso.
source: UPPCS (Pre.) Re-exam. 2015 · General Science & Technology GS p.286

subject: Science & Technology
question: Pneumoconiosis afflicts the workers who work mainly in :
explanation: Pneumoconiosis is a respiratory disease caused by inhaling various type of dust, such as coal dust, silica dust, asbestos dust etc. Pneumoconiosis mostly affects workers who work in the mining and construction sectors and deal with soil, silica, coal dust and asbestos for long time period. Biology
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 2005) · General Science & Technology GS p.286

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which disease is caused by allergy?
explanation: Asthma disease is caused by allergy. Exposure to various irritants and substances that trigger allergies (allergens) can trigger signs and symptoms of asthma. Asthma triggers are different from person to person.
source: MPPSC (Pre) GS 1991 · General Science & Technology GS p.286

subject: Science & Technology
question: Brights disease affects which part of body?
explanation: Bright's disease is a chronic inflammation of the blood vessels in the kidney with protein, specifically albumin, in the urine. Blue baby syndrome affects heart and Jaundice damages liver. Malaria destroys spleen and blood platelets.
source: UPPCS (Pre.) G.S. 1991 · General Science & Technology GS p.286

subject: Science & Technology
question: Hysteria disease generally occurs in which group-
explanation: Hysterical fits are most usual in adolescent girls and young women. Symptoms of hysteria included partial paralysis, hallucinations, and nervousness. Other symptoms of hysteria include shortness of breath, anxiety, fainting, nervousness, insomnia, sexual forwardness and irritability.
source: UPPCS (Pre.) G.S. 1991 · General Science & Technology GS p.286

subject: Science & Technology
question: Oral submucous fibrosis is a disease caused by
explanation: Oral submucous fibrosis is a disease caused by consuming concomitant tobacco. Oral submucous fibrosis (OSF) is a chronic disease that produces scars, tissue fibrosis, and precancerous lesions. It frequently occurs in the buccal mucosa. OSF patients experience a severe burning sensation in the mouth after ingesting spicy foods. Other symptoms of OSF include dry mouth, pain, taste disorders, restricted tongue mobility, trismus, dysphagia, and altered tone.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. IInd Paper 2014 · General Science & Technology GS p.286

subject: Science & Technology
question: The 'mad cow' disease is caused by–
explanation: In modern medicine certain infectious neurological disease were found to be transmitted by an agent. consisting of abnormally folded protein. The agent was similar in size to viruses. These agents were called prions. The most notable disease caused by prions are Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) commonly known as Mad cow disease in cattle and its analogous variant Cr-Jacob disease (CJD) in human.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2009 · General Science & Technology GS p.287

subject: Science & Technology
question: Emphysema is a disease caused by environmental pollution and the affected organ of the body is:
explanation: Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which alveolar walls are damaged due to which respiratory surface is decreased. One of the major causes of this is cigarette smoking. Emphysema is most common in men between the ages of 50 and 70.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.287

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which get affected by jaundice?
explanation: Liver gets affected by jaundice. Jaundice is a condition in which the skin, sclera (whites of the eyes) and mucous membranes turn yellow. This yellow colour is caused by a high level of bilirubin, a yellow-orange bile pigment. Bile is fluid secreted by the liver. Bilirubin is formed from the breakdown of red blood cells. Jaundice is often a sign of a problem with the liver, gallbladder, or pancreas. Jaundice can occur when too much bilirubin builds up in the body. This may happen when there are too many red blood cells dying or breaking down and going to the liver or the liver is overloaded or damaged or the bilirubin from the liver is not able to properly move into the digestive tract.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2006 - 07 · General Science & Technology GS p.287

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
explanation: Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs. With pneumonia, the air sacs may fill with fluid or pus. The infection can be life-threatening to anyone, but particularly to infants, children and people over 65. Symptoms include a cough with phlegm or pus, fever, chills and difficulty in breathing. Antibiotics can treat many forms of pneumonia. Some forms of pneumonia can be prevented by vaccines. Glaucoma is a group of eye conditions that damage the optic nerve, the health of which is vital for good vision. Glaucoma is one of the leading causes of blindness for people over the age of 60. Jaundice is caused by a build-up of bilirubin in the blood and tissues of the body. Any condition that disrupts the movement of bilirubin from the blood to the liver and out of the body can cause jaundice. Diabetes is a metabolic disease that causes high blood sugar. Hormone insulin convert excess of glucose into glycogen which could be stored in the body. With diabetes, body either doesn't make enough insulin or can't effectively use the insulin it does make.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1996 · General Science & Technology GS p.287

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following pair is wrong?
explanation: Poliomyelitis, commonly shortened to polio, is an infectious disease caused by the poliovirus. In about 0.5 percent of cases, it moves from the gut to affect the central nervous system and there is muscle weakness resulting in a flaccid paralysis. This can occur over a few hours to a few days. It spreads through contaminated water and food. Rest options are correctly matched.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 1999 · General Science & Technology GS p.287

explanation: Leukemia is a type of cancer in which there is an abnormal increase in the number of white blood cells, known as Leucocytes. These are responsible for development of immune system in human body.
source: UPPCS (Pre.) G.S. 2016 · General Science & Technology GS p.287

subject: Science & Technology
question: What is fever?
explanation: Fever is also known as hyperthermia or pyrexia, or elevated temperature. It describes a body temperature that’s higher than normal. Normal body temperature is typically around 98.6°F (37°C). Fever occurs when a part of the brain called the hypothalamus shifts the set point of normal body temperature upward. A fever is not a disease. It is usually a sign that body is trying to fight an illness or infection which is expressed by inflammation of blood platelets.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S., 2010 · General Science & Technology GS p.288

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which condition in the body is called cancer?
options: Closure of formation of healthy cells to and simultaneously death
Toxic chemicals get collected in some part of the body and eventually lead to death. Biology
Uncontrolled multiplication of cells leading to suffocation of healthy cells and eventual death at the end.
Stopping of the brain and eventually death due to a wound or tumor in the body.
explanation: Cancer is a type of illness caused by abnormal growth of the cells in the body. The cells reproduce uncontrollably and cause metastases in the body. The accumulation of these cells causes the tumor to be benign and malignant tumors.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 1996 · General Science & Technology GS p.288

subject: Science & Technology
question: In some parts of India, consumption of underground water causes mottled teeth and bone damage. Which one of the following is responsible for this malady ?
explanation: In some parts of India, consumption of underground water causes mottled teeth and bone damage. Flouride ions is responsible for this malady. Fluoride is an important mineral that plays an important role in the formation of dental enamel and mineralization in the bone at the optimum level. But in the excessive amount, it adversely affects the bones, joints and causes fluorosis in teeth. Fluoride contamination cause flourosis. It is a disease which is defined by mottling of teeth, abnormal bones that "are liable to fracture because flourine replaces Ca2+ and" makes the bones brittle.
source: UPSC CAPF Exam. Ist 2009 · General Science & Technology GS p.288

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following is a major effect of long term consumption of drinking water containing little (less than 0.5 ppm) or no fluoride?
explanation: Low fluoride intake creates risk of dental caries, and tooth decay. Therefore, long term consumption of drinking water with less than 0.5 ppm or no fluoride will cause cavity of tooth.
source: UPSC CAPF Exam. Ist 2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.288

subject: Science & Technology
question: Itai-Itai disease is caused by chronic poisoning of–
explanation: Itai-Itai disease is caused by chronic poisoning of cadmium (cd). Itai-itai disease is the most severe form of chronic Cd poisoning caused by prolonged oral Cd ingestion. Cadmium toxicity occurs when a person breathes in high levels of cadmium from the air, or eats food or drinks water containing high levels of cadmium. The main target organ of Cd toxicity in itai-itai disease is the kidney, where injury is manifested by tubular and glomerular dysfunction. Renal dysfunction causes an insufficiency of active vitamin D, followed by bone injury consisting of a combination of osteomalacia and osteoporosis.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. IInd 2008 · General Science & Technology GS p.288

options: Minamata disease and Blue Baby Syndrome
explanation: Minamata disease and Blue Baby Syndrome diseases are caused by the consumption of water contaminated by mercury and nitrate respectively.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Excess of which of the following in the blood causes the 'Blue Baby Syndrome' disease?
explanation: Excess of nitrates in the blood causes the 'Blue Baby Syndrome' disease. The most common cause of blue baby syndrome is water contaminated with nitrates. After a baby drinks formula made with nitrate-rich water, the body converts the nitrates into nitrites. These nitrites bind to the hemoglobin in the body, forming methemoglobin, which is unable to carry oxygen. The most common symptom of blue baby syndrome is a blue discolouration of the skin around the mouth, hands, and feet. This is also known as cyanosis and is a sign that the child or person is not getting enough oxygen.
source: MPPSC (Pre.) G.S. Ist Paper 2014 · General Science & Technology GS p.289

question: The well-known ‘bubble baby disease” is said to be because-
options: It is caused by water bubbles
The baby suffering from disease makes saliva bubbles
The sick child is treated in germ free plastic bubbles
This disease is cured with water bubbles only
explanation: Body suffering from severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) is vulnerable to infectious diseases thus need to stay in sterile environment or germ free plastic bubbles thus called as 'bubble baby disease.
source: UPPCS (Pre.) G.S. 1997 · General Science & Technology GS p.289

subject: Science & Technology
question: 'Silicosis' is a–
explanation: Silicosis is an interstitial lung disease caused by breathing in tiny bits of silica, a common mineral found in many types of rocks and soil. Over time, exposure to silica particles causes permanent lung scarring, called pulmonary fibrosis. When silica dust enters the lungs, it causes inflammation which over time leads to the development of scar tissue that makes breathing difficult. Cigarette smoking adds to the lung damage caused by silicosis. Complications from silicosis can include tuberculosis, lung cancer, chronic bronchitis, autoimmune disorders and kidney disease.
source: Uttarakhand UDA/LDA (Pre) 2006 · General Science & Technology GS p.289

Any condition that disrupts the movement of bilirubin from the blood to the liver and out of the body can cause jaundice. Cataract is eye defect, typhoid affects intestine and pneumonia affects lungs.

question: Which of the following diseases of Milch animals are infectious? 1. Foot and Mouth disease 2. Anthrax 3. Black Quarter 4. Cowpox Select the correct answer by using codes given below :
explanation: Foot and Mouth disease, Anthrax and Cowpox diseases of milch animals are infectious. Black Quarter is an acute, febrile, highly fatal disease of livestock especially in horse and sheep caused by Clostridium chauvoei and characterized by emphysematous swelling, commonly affecting heavy muscles. It is also an infectious disease.
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 2005) · General Science & Technology GS p.289

subject: Science & Technology
question: Emetophobia is the fear of :
explanation: Emetophobia is an intense, irrational fear of vomiting including fear of feeling nausea, seeing or hearing another person vomit, or seeing vomitus itself. It is an anxiety disorder that may occur alongside other mental health conditions, such as generalized anxiety disorder and obsessive-compulsive disorder.
source: Haryana PCS (Pre) 2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.290

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following pairs is/are not correct? Choose from the codes given below: 1. Chicken Pox-Virus 2. Diphtheria - Virus 3. Athlete's foot-Fungus 4. Meningitis - Protozoan Codes:
explanation: Chicken Pox is highly contagious disease caused by Varicella- Zoster herpes virus. Diphtheria is a serious infection caused by strains of bacteria called ‘Corynebacterium diphtheriae’ that make toxin (poison). Athlete's foot (tinea pedis) is fungal infection that usually begins between the toes. The fungus that caused athlete's foot is called Trichophyton. Meningitis is typically caused by an infection with microorganisms. Hence, Option (2) and (4) are not correctly matched.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which of the following are associated with diabetes mellitus, a common disease in adults? 1 . Higher sugar level in blood 2 . Lower sugar level in blood 3 . Lower insulin level in blood 4 . Higher insulin level in blood Select the correct answer using codes given below: Code :
explanation: Insulin is normally secreted by the beta cells (a type of islet cell of the pancreas). The stimulus for insulin secretion is a high blood glucose. Although there is always a low level of insulin secreted by the pancreas, the amount secreted into the blood increases as the blood glucose rises. Similarly, as blood glucose falls, the amount of insulin secreted by the pancreatic islets goes down. The pancreas secretes insulin and glucagon. Both hormones work in balance to play a vital role in regulating blood sugar levels. Lower insulin level in blood and higher sugar level in blood are associated with Diabetes mellitus, a common disease in adults.

To do so, they need help from Rhizobium bacteria. These special bacteria sitimulate the growth of nodules on the roots of leguminous plants. Rajma is an example of beans.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Nitrogen fixing bacteria make combination with cells of the roots of
explanation: Nitrogen fixation is the essential biological process and the initial stage of the nitrogen cycle. In this process, the free nitrogen available in the atmosphere is converted into ammonia by certain bacterial species like Rhizobium, Azotobacter, etc. and the complete process is carried on by natural phenomena. Rhizobium infects the roots of leguminous plants. They are usually found in the soil and produce nodules after infecting the roots of the leguminous plants. As a result, nitrogen gas is fixed from the atmosphere. This nitrogen is made available to the plants that help in their growth and development. When the legume dies there will be a breakdown of nodules. As a result, Rhizobium is released back to the cell where it can infect a new host.
source: UPPCS (Pre), 2019 · General Science & Technology GS p.305

explanation: Biological Nitrogen Fixation (BNF) is the term used for a process in which nitrogen gas (N₂) from the atmosphere is incorporated into the tissue of certain plants. Blue Green Algae (Cyanobacteria) are a special group of prokaryotes. BGA are widely distributed all over the earth. While fixing carbon from CO₂ , certain BGA can fix nitrogen (N₂) from the atmosphere, and are called nitrogen-fixing BGA, including free living and symbiotic forms.

explanation: Plants in the legume family are called Leguminous plants. They have nodules in their roots that contain nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Legumes are in symbiotic association with nitrogen-fixing bacteria called Rhizobia. These bacteria invade root hairs of leguminous plants and forms root nodules in which they fix nitrogen. A red pigment present in the root nodules of leguminous plants is known as Leghaemoglobin. Leghaemoglobin is an oxygen carrier molecule. It protects nitrogen- fixing enzyme nitrogenase from the side effect of oxygen as the enzyme is highly sensitive to oxygen.

question: Photosynthesis occurs in–
explanation: Photosynthesis can be split into two diffeent types of reaction:- (i) The Light reactions whereby sunlight is used as energy and create ATP and NADPH. This process takes place in the grana of chloroplasts in the presence of light. The Light reaction is faster than the Dark reaction. (ii) The Dark reactions are not directly light driven but are dependent on the products of light reactions (ATP and NADPH). In this reaction, carbon dioxide and water are broken down using ATP and NADPH into sugar as food for the plant. Biology 31 It is clear from above that the Light reactions of photosynthesis that create energy from sunlight can only occur during the day, but the Dark reactions (Calvin cycle) can occur both in day and night. So we can say that, photosynthesis occurs in Day or Night.

They have the mechanism to convert atmospheric nitrogen into a form that the crop plants can absorb readily
They induce the roots of the crop plants to absorb the soil nitrates in larger quantities.
explanation: Biofertilizers are organism that enrich the nutrient quality of soil. The main source of biofertilizers are Bacteria, Fungi and Cyanobacteria. The nodules on the roots of leguminous plants are formed by symbiotic association of Rhizobium. These bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen into organic forms which is used by the plant as nutrient. They alleviate the body's pain and inflammation
They act as immunosuppressants in the body.
They protect the body from the diseases caused by pathogens.
explanation: The overall ability of the body to fight the disease causing organisms (pathogens), conferred by the immune system is called immunity. The primary and secondary immune responses are carried out with the help of two special types of lymphocytes present in our blood, i.e., B-lymphocytes (B-cells) and T- lymphocytes (T-cells). Thus, both B-cells and T-cells are responsible for acquired immunity. B-cells are responsible for antibody-mediated immunity response. T-cells are responsible for cell-mediated immunity response. B cells produce antibodies to fight with the pathogens into our blood. The T-cells themselves do not secrete antibodies but help B cells to produce them. Hence option (d) is the correct answer.

question: Cryopreservation is a technique which encompasses the use of :
explanation: Cryopreservation is a technique to keep living cells and cells protected for a long time. In this technique, the substances are kept between −80 ° C to −196 ° C and dry ice or liquid nitrogen is used. All types of chemical activity cease in low temperature and cells can be protected. Extremely low temperatures can make ice in cells, so in this technique a layer of substances called cryo-protectants is used to protect the cells to be protected. Commercially, it is used to conserve the female eggs and sperm of men and is used for research on fungus, bacteria etc.
source: ACF/RFO (Mains) IInd 2018 · General Science & Technology GS p.326

subject: Science & Technology
question: In animals; nutrition, respiration and synthesis are three main properties of :
explanation: In animals; nutrition, respiration and synthesis are three main properties of metabolism. Anabolism and catabolism are the two broad classes of biochemical reactions that make up metabolism. Anabolism is the synthesis of complex molecules from simpler ones. These chemical reactions require energy. Catabolism is the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler ones.These reactions release energy.

explanation: The longest bone of the human body is the femur and the shortest stapes. Cholera is a bacterial disease caused by Vibrio cholerae. Athlete's foot disease is a fungal infection that affects the upper layer of the skin of the foot, especially when it is warm, moist and irritated.The fungus that causes athlete’s foot is called Trichophyton and is commonly found on floors and in clothing. Hence, staterment 1 and 2 are correct.

subject: Science & Technology
question: Aspartame is an artificial sweetner sold in the market. It consists of amino acids and provides calories like other amino acids. Yet, it is used as a low calorie sweetening agent in food items. What is the basis of this use?
options: Aspartame is as sweet as table sugar, but unlike table sugar, it is not readily oxidized in human body due to lack of requisite enzymes.
When aspartame is used in food processing, the sweet taste remains, but it becomes resistant to oxidation.
Aspartame is as sweet as sugar, but after ingestion into the body, it is converted into the body, it is converted into metabolites that yield no calories.
Aspartame is several times sweeter than table sugar, hence food items made with small quantities of aspartame yield fewer calories on oxidation.
explanation: Aspartame is an artificial sweetner sold in the market. It consists of amino acids and provides calories like other amino acids. The basis of aspartame use is that it is several times sweeter than table sugar, hence food items made with small quantities of aspartame yield fewer calories on oxidation.
source: (IAS (Pre) Ist Paper G.S. 2011) · General Science & Technology GS p.327

question: Consider the following statements? 1 . The Earth's magnetic field has reversed every few hundred thousand years. 2 . explanation: There was a lack of oxygen in the atmosphere at the time of the creation of the Earth. Ice is best conducter of heat

question: The percentage of water in an adult human body is approximate–
explanation: The percentage of water in an adult human body is approximate 65 to 70%. Water is a vital nutrient to the life of every cell, acts first as a building material. The brain and heart are composed of 73% water, and the lungs are about 83% water. The skin contains 64% water, muscles and kidneys are 79%, and even the bones are watery 31%. It regulates our internal body temperature by sweating and respiration. The carbohydrates and proteins that our bodies use as food are metabolized and transported by water in the bloodstream. It assists in flushing waste mainly through urination and acts as a shock absorber for brain, spinal cord, and fetus forms saliva. It lubricates joints.

question: Which of the following are the reasons for the occurrence of multi-drug resistance in- microbial pathogens in India? explanation: Overuse and misuse of antimicrobial agents is the single most important cause of development of resistance. For instance, when antibiotics (which are meant for bacterial infections only) are taken by people with viral infections like cold and flu. They are also used indiscriminately as growth promoters in animals or used to prevent diseases in healthy animals. Poor infection control practices in hospitals, in the hospitality sector, and at home can cause the spread of disease, fuelling the high use of these drugs. question: Chandrayaan-2 was a mixture of success and set-back. Which of the following statements are applicable to Chandrayaan-2 mission? 1. It aimed at exploring South Pole of the moon. 2. The location of crash landing of Vikram has later been identified.
explanation: Chandrayaan-2 is the second lunar mission of India after the success of Chandrayaan-1. Chandrayaan- 2 Mission was launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre on July 22, 2019, by GSLV MK III-MI. The main aim of Chandrayaan-2 was to trace the location and abundance of lunar water on the moon's surface. The mission targeted the "South Pole region" of the moon which was completely unexplored. The Chandrayaan-2 mission consisted of three main modules: 1. Lunar orbiter 2. Vikram lander (for soft landing on the surface of the moon and to relay information to earth)

explanation: Black hole is a place in space, from which even light too can not escape, and there are many type of black hole: steller intermediate, super massive and miniature black hole. Like most stars, during the main phase of its lifetime the sun creates energy by fusing hydrogen atoms in its core. In about a billions of year the sun will start to run out of hydrogen in its core to fuse and it will begin to collapse.

question: With reference to India’s satellite launch vehicles, consider the following statements: 1 . Satellites launched by PSLV appear to remain permanently fixed in the same position in the sky, as viewed from a particular location on Earth 3 . Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: The Geosynchronous satellite launch vehicle Mark-III (GSLV MK-III) is a 3 stage medium lift launch vehicle developed by ISRO. It is designed to launch satellites into geostationary orbit and is intended as a launch vehicle for future India's crewed space mission hence statement (3) is wrong. PSLV primarily used for launching remote sensing satellites into sun-synchronous polar orbit, but it can also launch satellite of 1350 kg in Geo transfer orbit (GTO). Hence statement (2) is for launching heavier communicational satellite into GTO, but can also launch satellites into LEO (Lower Earth Orbit) while PSLV is used for earth resources monitoring. Hence statement (1) is correct.

question: Consider the following statements: A person in a spaceship located half way between the earth and the sun will notice that the 1. Sky is jet black. 2. Stars do not twinkle. 3. Temperature outside the spaceship is much higher than that on the surface of the earth. Of these statements
explanation: There is a presence of atmosphere at earth's surface which consists of thick and moving layer of air the dust particles, particulates, smog, water vapour and smoke are also present is air. Stars twinkle when we see them from the earth's surface because we are viewing them through thick layer of turbulent (moving) air in the earth's atmosphere. As their light travel through the many layers of earth's atmosphere, the light of stars is bent (refracted) many time in random direction. This random refraction results in Science Technology 35 the twinkling of stars, but for a person in spaceship no such refraction takes place (because space is vacuum). Thus star will not twinkle Similarly, sky will appear blue to us due to Rayleigh scattering which is again due to presence of atmosphere. As scattering phenomenon is absent in space hence sky appears black. Temperature outside the spaceship is higher in comparison to earth's surface because of being nearer to sun. 50 . subject: Science & Technology
question: In which generation of computers, transistors were used?
explanation: A transistor computer, now often called a second generation computer, is a computer which uses discrete transistors instead of vacuum tubes. The first generation of electronic computers used vacuum tubes, which generated large amounts of heat, were bulky and unreliable. A second generation of computers, through the late 1950s and 1960s featured circuit boards filled with individual transistors and magnetic core memory. The period of third generation was from 1965-1971. The computers of third generation used Integrated Circuits (ICs) in place of transistors. A single IC has many transistors, resistors, and capacitors along with the associated circuitry. The IC was invented by Jack Kilby. The period of fourth generation was from 1971- 1980. Computers of fourth generation used Very Large Scale Integrated (VLSI) circuits. VLSI circuits having about 5000 transistors and other circuit elements with their associated circuits on a single chip.

Multitasking automatically interrupts the running program, saving its state (partial results, memory contents and computer register contents) and loading the saved state of another program and transferring control to it.

question: 'RNA interference (RNAi)' technology has gained popularity in the last few years. Why? 1. It is used in developing gene silencing therapies. 2. It can be used in developing therapies for the treatment of cancer. 3. It can be used to develop hormone replacement therapies 4. It can be used to produce crop plants that are resistant to viral pathogens. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: RNA interference (RNAi) technology is a biological process in which RNA molecules inhibit gene expression or translation, by neutralizing targeted mRNA molecules. Historically it was also known as - co-suppression, post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS) and quelling. With the invention of Science Technology 40 synthetically made small interfering RNA, it became possible to silence the specific gene sequences instead of silencing the entire gene- RNAi has also been used to target specific gene sequences that can cause cancer therefore it is helpful in developing therapies for cancer treatment. RNAi has proven to be very effective for controlling plant virus diseases for many different viruses in many plant species. For example, Genetically engineered papaya ringspot virus (PRSV)- resistant papaya, which was developed and used in Hawai when no other options for controlling PRSV were available. Hormone replacement therapy is a form of hormone therapy used to treat symptoms associated with female menopause and RNAi does not have a role to play in it. Therefore only statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct.

Like many other organic molecules that are made inside living cells, DNA can also by synthesized in test tubes using the tools of organic chemistry. In most descriptions of DNA synthesis technology, we hear that DNA sequences can be made by simply adding together the A's T's C's and G's ......the ''bases'' that make the rungs of the twisted DNA ladder. Hence option (b) is correct. Given appropriate surroundings, most plant as animal cells can live multiply and even express differentiated properties in a tissue culture dish. The cell can be watched continuously under the microscope and the effect of adding and removing specific molecules can be explored. By mixing two cell types, the interactions between one cell type and another can be studied. Hence option (c and d) are correct. Option (a) is not correct because functional chromosomes can not be created by joining segments of DNA taken from cells of different species.

subject: Science & Technology
question: M 1. Consider the following statements: 1. Other than those made by humans, nanoparticles do not exist in nature. 2. Nanoparticles of some metallic oxides are used in the manufacture of some cosmetics. 3. Nanoparticles of some commercial products which enter the environment are unsafe for humans. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Nanoparticles are incredibly tiny particles of a given substance. Nanoparticles are less than 100 nanometers thick. To give some perspective, a nanometer is 1000 times smaller than the thickness of one strand of hair. Nanoparticles can be naturally created, for example, minuscule droplets of sea spray. However, most nanoparticles are created in the lab. For sunscreen, the nanoparticles are zinc oxide and titanium dioxide. These ingredients are broken down into ultrafine particles before being added to sunscreen. So, statement 1 is not correct and statement 2 is correct. Inhaled particulate matter can be deposited throughout the human respiratory tract, and an important fraction of inhaled nanoparticles deposit in the lungs. Nanoparticles can potentially move from the lungs to other organs such as the brain, the liver, the spleen and possibly the foetus in pregnant women. So, statement 3 is correct. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer. 2. subject: Science & Technology
question: With reference to Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs), consider the following statements: 1. They enable the digital representation of physical assets. 2. They are unique cryptographic tokens that exist on a blockchain. 3. They can be traded or exchanged at equivalency and therefore can be used as a medium of commercial transactions. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Non-fungible tokens, often referred to as NFTs, are blockchain-based tokens that each represent a unique asset like a piece of art, digital content, or media. An NFT can be thought of as an irrevocable digital certificate of ownership and authenticity for a given asset, whether digital or physical. They cannot be traded or exchanged at equivalency and therefore, cannot be used as a medium of commercial transactions.
source: UPSC IAS 2022 · General Science & Technology GS p.406
